# Pi sweep review — CastCircle

Exhaustive per-file pass: 281 code files across 156 batches — model ds4/GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2:off — 2026-08-29.

## Findings

- [medium] lib/data/database/app_database.dart:130-142 — `_step` swallows the benign "already applied" case but its error classification relies on raw SQLite/drift message text (`'duplicate column name'`, `'already exists'`), which drift may localize or reword across versions — a real failure could then be silently swallowed and the migration "succeeds" while the column/index is missing, and every later query dies with "no such column" forever (the exact failure the doc comment warns about) — match on the exception type (e.g. drift's `InvalidSchemaException`/`SqlException` with a known code) or add a version-guard check (`migrator.columnExists`) before each add so the benign case is detected structurally rather than by message text.
- [medium] lib/data/database/app_database.dart:146-188 — migration steps are guarded by `from < N` but each step is not idempotent-checked; if a user upgrades from v1 to v7 in one jump and one step fails mid-way (e.g. index creation at 169-181), the next launch re-runs all steps from the same `from` value and `_step`'s message-text matching (see previous finding) decides whether the already-created index is tolerated — add per-step existence checks (`migrator.indexExists`/`columnExists`) so each step is independently idempotent.
- [medium] lib/data/database/app_database.dart:262-273 — `insertRecording` deletes prior rows only when `entry.productionId.present && entry.scriptLineId.present`, but the subsequent `insertOrReplace` still inserts a row whose `id` is the random primary key; if either field is absent the delete is skipped and duplicate rows for the same line pile up silently (the exact pile-up the doc comment describes) — require both fields (assert/throw) or fall back to deleting by `scriptLineId` alone when `productionId` is absent.
- [low] lib/data/database/app_database.dart:119 — `AppDatabase.forTesting(super.e)` is a named constructor that takes a `QueryExecutor` but the class's own `_openConnection()` is still used by the default constructor; the testing entry point is unreachable from the file list and its existence suggests tests construct the DB differently than production, hiding the WAL/busy_timeout setup (316-334) from test coverage — consider a factory that routes both paths through the same `setup` pragmas, or drop the constructor if unused.
- [low] lib/data/database/app_database.dart:316-334 — `_openConnection` is a top-level function (not a static member of `AppDatabase`), so it is part of the library's public surface even though only the default constructor uses it; wrapping it in a private helper or making it a static private member keeps the public API of the file minimal.
- [medium] lib/data/models/cast_member_model.dart:10-13 — `CastRole.fromString` degrades unknown role strings to `CastRole.primary` silently; a malformed or newer-version row (e.g. `'director'`, `'stage_manager'`) becomes a primary cast member with no signal, and `hasJoined`/UI logic that treats `primary` differently from `organizer`/`understudy` will misclassify the member — log/flag the unknown value (or return a nullable/`unknown` role) so the degradation is observable instead of silent.
- [low] lib/data/models/cast_member_model.dart:48-70 — `copyWith` accepts `userId`, `contactInfo`, `invitedAt`, `joinedAt` as nullable parameters but cannot clear them back to null (passing `null` keeps the old value); a member who leaves/joins again cannot reset `joinedAt`/`userId` via `copyWith` — use a sentinel (e.g. `Object? userId = _unset`) or explicit `clearUserId` helpers if callers need to unset.
- [low] lib/data/models/cast_member_model.dart:46 — `hasJoined => userId != null` conflates "has a user id" with "has joined"; `joinedAt` is the actual join marker and `userId` may be set before the member accepts the invite — if callers rely on this for gating (assumed: cast UI/invite flow not in this batch), rename to `hasUser` or compare `joinedAt != null` to avoid a lying name.
- [low] lib/data/database/app_database.dart:33-34,60-62,96-97 — several columns default to `const Constant('')` (empty string) rather than `nullable()`; empty-string-as-missing means callers cannot distinguish "no act/scene/location" from "act/scene/location is the empty string", and `linesInAct` (script_models.dart:378-380) filters `l.act == act` so a literal `''` query would match every defaulted row — prefer nullable columns or document the sentinel; this is a schema-level maintainability trap, not a runtime bug.
- [low] lib/data/database/app_database.dart:204 — `insertProduction` uses `InsertMode.insertOrReplace`, so an insert with a colliding `id` silently replaces the existing production row (and its cast/lines/scenes/recordings become orphans referencing a replaced id) — prefer `insertOrReplace` only for explicit upsert paths and a plain insert (or `OrReplace` with a uniqueness check) elsewhere; assumed: callers in production_providers.dart (not in this batch) rely on replace semantics.
- [low] lib/data/database/app_database.dart:304-305 — `insertCastMember` also uses `insertOrReplace` on a random-`id` table; re-inviting the same character/user inserts a second row rather than updating the existing one unless callers pass the same `id` — same class as the recording pile-up at 262-273 but with no delete-first guard; verify callers always pass a stable `id` or switch to an upsert keyed on (productionId, characterName/userId).
- [info] lib/data/database/app_database.dart:10 — `part 'app_database.g.dart';` references a generated part file not present in this batch; the `_$AppDatabase` supertype and companion classes (`ProductionsCompanion`, etc.) are assumed to exist there — verify the generated file is committed/generated at build time, otherwise the file does not compile.
- [info] lib/data/models/cast_member_model.dart:7-9 — doc comment claims Supabase role strings use `'actor'` for primary; this is asserted only by the code itself (no Supabase schema in this batch) — verify against the actual Supabase column values before trusting the mapping.

- [medium] lib/data/services/audio_level_service.dart:60-62 — LRU cap evicts the oldest-inserted entry, not the least-recently-used one, and eviction happens before the new insert so a hot path can be evicted while stale paths linger — cache thrash under >512 distinct paths re-runs the loudness MethodChannel per playback — maintain a proper access-ordered LRU (e.g. LinkedHashMap with re-insert on hit) or use a simple bounded map with touch-on-read.
- [medium] lib/data/services/audio_level_service.dart:36-64 — `volumeFor` caches a fallback 1.0 result on every failure path (channel missing, decode failure, non-finite/non-negative rms), so a transient failure is pinned for the lifetime of the cache entry and `prefetch`/`invalidate` can't distinguish it — only cache successful analyses (or store a sentinel and retry on failure) so a later call can re-attempt.
- [low] lib/data/services/audio_level_service.dart:68-70 — `prefetch` is fire-and-forget but the returned Future is discarded with no error handling; an unhandled async error from `volumeFor` (it catches internally, but any future refactor that throws before the try, e.g. on `_gainCache` mutation races) would crash the zone — keep the future and attach a no-op catch, or document the swallow.
- [low] lib/data/services/audio_level_service.dart:30,63 — `_gainCache` is mutated from `prefetch`'s async continuation without synchronization; concurrent `volumeFor` calls for the same path can both miss the cache and both invoke the channel, doubling work and racing the eviction check — guard with a per-path in-flight future or a lock.

- [low] lib/data/services/analytics_service.dart:10-11 — `_analytics` getter re-evaluates `firebaseAvailable` on every call; if that flag flips mid-session (init order), events logged before availability are silently dropped with no queue/retry — resolve once at first use and document the drop, or buffer events until available.
- [low] lib/data/services/analytics_service.dart:33,60 — optional parameters are conditionally included via `if (x != null)` inside map literals; FirebaseAnalytics parameter maps with null-typed values are fine here, but the pattern silently omits the key rather than sending a default, making downstream dashboards unable to distinguish "absent" from "zero" — send an explicit default (e.g. 0) or document the omission contract.

## Coverage
lib/features/cast_manager/cast_manager_screen.dart — findings: 24
- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:122-139 — `_memoAssignment` caches by a key that includes `_genderOverrides.toString()` but the cache is never invalidated when `_overrides` changes, and the memoized result is computed inside `build` via a spread over `script.characters` — a stale cache returns assignments computed under a previous preset/gender state after a preset change that only updates `_currentPreset` via `setState` — consequence: character tiles show the wrong voice after switching preset until a full reload — fix: include `_overrides` in the cache key or clear `_assignmentCache` in the preset `onChanged` before `setState`.
- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:125-127 — `Object.hash(identityHashCode(script.lines), ...)` uses `identityHashCode` on a list plus `Object.hash` truncation to build a cache key — two different scripts whose lists share identity (e.g. a copyWith that reuses the same `lines` list) or hash collisions silently reuse a stale assignment map — consequence: wrong voice shown for characters after a script refresh — fix: key on a stable script identity (e.g. `script.title` + line count + first/last line ids) instead of `identityHashCode`.

- [medium] lib/features/cast_manager/voice_config_screen.dart:383 — preview sample text `'To be, or not to be...'` is a hard-coded literal used as the TTS probe — consequence: any voice that fails only on this exact string (e.g. a voice lacking English phonemes) is validated with a sentence unrelated to the script's language — fix: preview the character's own first line from `script.lines` instead of a fixed quote.

- [medium] lib/features/join/join_production_screen.dart:566-569 — voice preset is read from `_foundProduction!['voice_preset']` and persisted unconditionally after the join succeeded, but if `VoiceConfigService.instance.setPreset` throws it is caught by the outer catch (line 580) which reports "Failed to join" even though the join itself already succeeded — consequence: user sees a failure for a cosmetic preset write and may retry, double-joining — fix: wrap the preset write in its own try/catch (or move it before the success path) so preset errors don't masquerade as join failures.
- [medium] lib/features/join/join_production_screen.dart:245-251 — the "Join without a character" `RadioListTile` is rendered even when `_castMembers` is null (i.e. before the roster loads), and its `groupValue`/`onChanged` write `_selectedCharacter = '__none__'` while `_joinProduction` (line 457) treats `'__none__'` as an empty character name — consequence: a user can tap it during the roster-loading window and submit a join with an empty character before unclaimed invitations were ever fetched, racing the claim path — fix: gate the tile behind `_castMembers != null` like the character list.
- [low] lib/features/join/join_production_screen.dart:210,516,524,525 — repeated `as String? ??` casts on `_foundProduction!` map keys (`title`, `organizer_id`, `created_at`, `join_code`, `locale`, `voice_preset`) with no shared accessor; a schema drift in the lookup RPC payload (e.g. `join_code` renamed) silently yields null/'' with no error — consequence: production row saved locally with empty organizer/locale and no compile-time safety — fix: add a typed `Production`-from-map factory (or a small `_field()` helper) used at every site.
- [low] lib/features/join/join_production_screen.dart:361-364 — magic number `6` (join-code length) duplicated with the `maxLength: 6` at line 158 and the hint 'H4MK7P'; if the code length ever changes, three sites must move in lockstep — consequence: validation and UI drift apart silently — fix: hoist a `static const joinCodeLength = 6` and use it in all three places.
- [medium] lib/features/onboarding/model_setup_screen.dart:127-235 — `_downloadAll` is a god function (~110 lines) handling consent pref, analytics, sequential downloads, listener-driven progress, timeout polling, and per-item error mapping in one body — consequence: the Android/iOS branches and the matching-branch each have their own error semantics, making a partial-failure state (one item ready, one errored) hard to reason about and easy to regress — fix: split into `_downloadVoices()` and `_downloadMatching()` helpers with a shared error funnel.
- [medium] lib/features/onboarding/model_setup_screen.dart:163-171 — the timeout-poll loop `while (mounted && !_voices.ready && _voices.error == null)` busy-polls every 500 ms for up to 15 minutes with no cancellation when the user leaves the screen except via `mounted`; if the widget is disposed the loop exits only on the next tick, and the deadline error is written to `_voices.error` on a dead state object — consequence: wasted timer work and a state write after dispose in the edge case where `mounted` flips between the check and the write — fix: guard the deadline write with `if (mounted)` and add an early `break` when `!mounted`.
- [medium] lib/features/onboarding/model_setup_screen.dart:130-131 — consent pref `models_auto_download_ok` is set to `true` unconditionally at the start of `_downloadAll`, before any download actually succeeds; the comment says the auto-downloader "only runs for users who chose to download", but a user who taps Download-all and then immediately gets a network error has already granted the auto-download flag — consequence: next launch auto-starts a large (~180 MB) download the user never completed, on cellular potentially — fix: set the pref only after the downloads settle successfully (or set it to the outcome, not a constant true).
- [low] lib/features/onboarding/model_setup_screen.dart:59-65 — `_matching` is Android-only via `Platform.isAndroid`, but `_onServiceState` (line 103) early-returns on Android, so the listener that mirrors native progress is effectively iOS-only while `_downloadAll`'s iOS branch (line 153-157) relies on that same listener for completion — consequence: on iOS the loop at 164 depends on `_voices.ready` being set by `_onServiceState`, which only fires if the service listener fires; if the service never emits (e.g. download already complete before listener attach), the loop spins to the 15-minute deadline — fix: seed `_voices.ready` from `svc.getState(...)` before entering the wait loop.
- [low] lib/features/onboarding/model_setup_screen.dart:229-234 — `context.pop()` after the success toast is called without checking `mounted` after the async `showAutoToast`; if the screen was disposed during the toast, `context.pop()` throws a "deactivated widget" error — consequence: crash on the success path in the dispose-during-toast race — fix: `if (mounted) context.pop();` (or use the navigator-aware mounted check).
- [low] lib/features/onboarding/model_setup_screen.dart:27-37 — `maybeOffer` checks `context.mounted` only after the two awaits (line 35) but performs `prefs.setBool('model_setup_offered', true)` before that check; if the context is dead the pref is still stamped, so the screen is never offered again even though it was never shown — consequence: a new user who backgrounded the app during the pref write permanently loses the one-time setup offer — fix: move `setBool` after the `context.mounted`/push decision, or set it only once the screen is actually shown.

- [medium] lib/features/script_editor/validation_panel.dart:135-136 — `passCount == checks.length` is computed from a local list that may be empty — when `validateScript` returns zero checks (currently impossible but reachable if callers pass a script whose lines/scenes are all absent and a future refactor drops a check), `allPassed` is true and the header claims "Script looks good!" with no evidence — guard with `checks.isNotEmpty && passCount == checks.length`.

- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroMLXService.swift:336-339 — `pruneScheduled` is read/written via instance method but declared `private static var`, and the guard/flag pair races across instances — consequence: two service instances (or a re-init after unload) can both pass the `guard !Self.pruneScheduled` check before either sets it, launching duplicate prune passes that double-remove entries and log misleading counts; smallest safe fix: make `pruneScheduled` an instance `private var` guarded by `genLock`, or set it inside the lock before the async hop.
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroMLXService.swift:171,337 — `pruneCacheIfNeeded()` is called synchronously on the synthesis path before the cache-hit check, but the prune body runs on a detached global-utility queue with no completion signal — consequence: a first-call cache miss can race the prune's directory enumeration, and a WAV written during enumeration can be deleted before its LRU date is touched, silently dropping a just-created cache entry; smallest safe fix: schedule the prune once from `init()`/first `loadModel()` rather than inline on every synthesis miss, or capture the write path and skip it in the removal loop.
- [low] ios/Runner/KokoroMLXService.swift:200 — language is derived from `voice.hasPrefix("a")` only, so any non-`a` voice (e.g. a future `jp_*`/`kr_*`/`zh_*` Kokoro voice) silently synthesizes with `.enGB` phonemes — consequence: wrong-language G2P produces garbled audio with no error surfaced; smallest safe fix: switch on the full two-letter prefix and throw `voiceNotFound` for unsupported prefixes.
- [low] ios/Runner/KokoroMLXService.swift:284-291 — `vDSP_vclip` clamps to [-1,1] then `vsmul` scales by `Int16.max`, but `vfix16` is applied to already-Int16-cast values with no round-half-to-even control — consequence: clipping asymmetry (positive samples saturate at 32767 while negatives reach -32768) yields a slight DC offset on loud material; smallest safe fix: clip to [-1, 0.9999695…] or scale by `Int16.max/2` symmetrically before the cast.
- [info] ios/Runner/KokoroMLXService.swift:329-331 — cache directory is resolved from `.cachesDirectory` at synthesis time but `modelDirectory` uses `.documentDirectory`; iOS may purge `Caches/` under storage pressure without the LRU prune knowing — consequence: cached WAVs vanish mid-session and every line re-synthesizes at full GPU cost; smallest safe fix: verify existence before the cache-hit return and fall through to synthesis on miss (the code already does this via `fileExists`, so treat as informational only).
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/Albert/AlbertEmbeddings.swift:29-30 — `layerNorm.bias![0...]`/`weight![0...]` force-unwraps optional MLX parameter buffers and assign the whole range in place; if the vendored `LayerNorm` init ever leaves bias/weight nil (e.g. a weights file missing `LayerNorm.weight`), the crash is a force-unwrap trap rather than the intended `fatalError` guard at line 22 — consequence: a corrupt safetensors file crashes with an EXC_BAD_INSTRUCTION instead of the caught `modelCorrupt` path in KokoroMLXService.swift:113-118, defeating the delete-and-redownload recovery; smallest safe fix: guard `layerNorm.bias != nil && layerNorm.weight != nil` alongside the shape check and `fatalError` there.
- [low] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/Albert/AlbertEmbeddings.swift:15-17 — `weights[...]!` force-unwraps three embedding weight keys with no presence check — consequence: a safetensors file missing any `bert.embeddings.*_embeddings.weight` key crashes at model load instead of surfacing `modelCorrupt`; smallest safe fix: `guard` all three keys and `fatalError` (or throw) before constructing the `Embedding`s.

- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/Decoder/MLXSTFT.swift:36 — `MLX.where(pDiff .> 0, intervalHigh, pDiffMod)` passes a scalar `intervalHigh` as the value branch of a where over an array condition — if the MLX overload requires array branches this either fails to compile or silently broadcasts a constant; the phase-unwrap "add 2π when discontinuity" branch is exactly the path that must fire — consequence: unwrapped phase can be wrong (aliasing 2π jumps) and the istft reconstruction drifts — smallest safe fix: build the branch as an MLXArray broadcast (`MLXArray(intervalHigh)` / `MLXArray(pDiffMod)`) so both branches are arrays.
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/Decoder/MLXSTFT.swift:38 — `MLX.where(pDiffMod .== intervalLow, ddSignArray, pDiffMod)` compares a float array to a scalar with `.==` and again feeds scalar/array branches — float equality on a computed value is fragile and the branch types are inconsistent — consequence: the equality branch almost never fires (float ==), so the ddSign correction is dead code and phase unwrap silently degrades — smallest safe fix: compare with a tolerance (`abs(pDiffMod - intervalLow) .< eps`) and use array-typed branches.
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/Decoder/MLXSTFT.swift:142 — `MLX.concatenated(Array(repeating: wSquared, count: t / winLen))` tiles `w*w` only `t/winLen` times, but the overlap-add loop at 149–163 needs the window-sum array to cover `t + winLen` samples (the last frame extends past `t`); `windowSumArray` is then truncated by `outputStride.shape[0]` at 151 — consequence: for inputs whose length is not an exact multiple of `winLen`, the final normalization denominator is zeros → division by zero / NaN tail in the reconstructed audio — smallest safe fix: tile `ceil(Float(t + winLen) / Float(winLen))` copies (or at least `t/winLen + 1`) and slice to the needed length.
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/Decoder/MLXSTFT.swift:150 — `output[.stride(from: i, by: windowModLen), .ellipsis]` strides the *time* axis by `windowModLen` (= winLen/hopLen), but overlap-add requires striding by `hopLen` positions per phase offset — with the shipped 800/200 config `windowModLen == 4` while the hop is 200, so the loop mixes samples 200 apart as if they were adjacent — consequence: the reconstructed waveform is scrambled/aliased whenever winLen ≠ hopLen·1, and even in the default config the phase-offset decomposition is wrong (should stride by hopLen, not by winLen/hopLen) — smallest safe fix: stride the output by `hopLen` (`output[.stride(from: i, by: hopLen), ...]`) and pad/trim accordingly.
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/Decoder/MLXSTFT.swift:173-175 — the trim uses `winLen / 2` on both ends but the istft was centered-padded by `nFft/2` in the forward pass (mlxStft pads `nFft/2` at line 91); when `winLength != filterLength` the trim removes the wrong guard band — consequence: reconstructed audio is offset/shorter than the input, misaligned with the original signal — smallest safe fix: trim by `filterLength / 2` (the forward pad amount) instead of `winLen / 2`.

- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/TTSEngine/TimestampPredictor.swift:33-34 — `left` is assigned `right` immediately after `right` is initialized from `dur[0]`, making the initial `left` value identical to `right` and discarding the intended distinct starting offset; consequence: the first token's start timestamp collapses to the end-of-preamble position, shifting all subsequent timestamps by the preamble duration and producing wrong audio alignment on every call; smallest safe fix: initialize `left` to `0` (or the intended preamble offset) and keep `right = 2 * max(0, dur[0] - 3)` without overwriting `left`.
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/TTSEngine/TimestampPredictor.swift:60,64 — timestamps are computed as `left / 80.0` where `left` accumulates frame counts, but the comment at lines 14-16 says the divisor should map frames to seconds at sample rate 24000 (i.e., divide by 40, or use 80 only for half-frames); consequence: emitted token start/end timestamps are scaled by the wrong factor, so downstream subtitle/word-timing consumers get values off by 2x; smallest safe fix: pick one consistent unit (frames vs half-frames) and divide by the matching constant (40 for frames→seconds at 24kHz), documenting it next to the constant.
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/TTSEngine/TimestampPredictor.swift:41-43 — the loop `break`s out of the token iteration when `i >= dur.count - 1` instead of `continue`ing or clamping, silently dropping all remaining tokens' timestamps once the index nears the end; consequence: trailing tokens get no `start_ts`/`end_ts`, so word-level timings are missing for the tail of long utterances; smallest safe fix: `continue` (or clamp `i`/`j` to `dur.count - 1`) so later tokens still get timestamps.
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/TTSEngine/TimestampPredictor.swift:56-57 — when `j >= dur.count` the loop `break`s rather than clamping `j` to the last valid index, dropping timestamps for the current and all remaining tokens; consequence: any token whose phoneme span touches the end of the duration array leaves the rest of the utterance untimed; smallest safe fix: clamp `j = min(j, dur.count - 1)` and continue instead of breaking.
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/TTSEngine/TimestampPredictor.swift:12 — `preditTimestamps` is a misspelling of `predictTimestamps` (missing 'c'), and the static method returns `Void` while mutating `MToken` fields (`t.start_ts`, `t.end_ts`) via inout-style side effects on array elements; consequence: callers must know the mutation is implicit and the typo propagates to every call site, hurting maintainability and inviting silent misuse; smallest safe fix: rename to `predictTimestamps(tokens:predictionDuration:)` and document the in-place mutation of `MToken`.
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/TTSEngine/TimestampPredictor.swift:31 — `TO_DO:` comment on a sensitive timing path documents an unresolved question about the `-3` offset (a magic number with no derivation); consequence: the correctness of the preamble trim stays unverified and the constant is easy to break during refactors; smallest safe fix: resolve or replace the TODO with a named constant + comment explaining why `-3` (e.g., `preambleFrameOffset = 3`).
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/TTSEngine/TimestampPredictor.swift:23 — magic divisor `80.0` is a bare local with no named constant or cross-file reference, and the same frame-rate math likely appears in sibling TTS files; consequence: changing sample rate or frame length in one place silently desyncs timestamps elsewhere; smallest safe fix: hoist `frameDivisor` into a shared TTS constant (e.g., `TTSEngineConstants`) used by both predictor and any duration/prosody code.

- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/TTSEngine/WeightLoader.swift:62-67,75-80,92-97 — the `weight_v` conditional-transpose block is copy-pasted three times across predictor, text_encoder, and decoder branches, and each copy already carries divergent surrounding handling (predictor also transposes F0/N projections, decoder also transposes noise_convs), so a future fix to the shape-check or transpose logic must be applied in three places; consequence: any divergence fix (e.g., correcting `checkArrayShape` usage or the transpose axes) will be missed in one branch, producing silently mis-shaped weights for one component only; smallest safe fix: extract a single `private static func sanitizeWeightV(_ key: String, _ value: MLXArray, into: inout [String: MLXArray])` helper and call it from all three branches.

- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/TTSEngine/WeightLoader.swift:36-104 — `loadWeights` is a god function: a single ~70-line static method owning disk load, four-way component dispatch, three transposition policies, and shape validation, with no decomposition; consequence: any change (new component, new rule) forces edits inside one monolithic method with high regression risk and no unit-testable seams; smallest safe fix: split into `loadRaw`, `sanitizeComponent(_:key:value:into:)`, and `checkArrayShape` (already separate) so each rule is independently testable.

- [low] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/TTSEngine/WeightLoader.swift:33-35 — doc comment references a past bug ("a `try!` here turned one truncated download into a crash") rather than current behavior; consequence: readers may assume a re-download/recovery path exists when the current code only `throws` and lets the caller handle it, with no retry guidance; smallest safe fix: rewrite the comment to describe present behavior ("throws on unreadable/corrupt weights; callers must handle re-download") and drop the historical anecdote.
- [medium] ios/Runner/KokoroVendored/TTSEngine/WeightLoader.swift:88 — `if key.contains("noise_convs"), key.hasSuffix(".weight")` uses Swift's implicit-AND comma form inside an `if` with no `else` fallthrough for keys matching only one condition; consequence: a decoder key like `...noise_convs.bias` or `...noise_convs.weight_v` falls to the later branches correctly, but a key matching `.weight` suffix without `noise_convs` also falls through — acceptable — yet the comma-AND form is easy to misread as an OR during maintenance, risking a wrong transpose being added; smallest safe fix: rewrite as `if key.contains("noise_convs") && key.hasSuffix(".weight")` for explicit AND semantics.

- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:121-124 — applyStress's stress==0/-0.5 and stress==0/0.5/1 branches overlap on `stress == 0`, so the first matching arm wins and the "no stress markers present → restress" path (line 124) is unreachable for stress==0 — consequence: a phonetic string with no stress markers and stress 0 never gets the secondary-stress prefix applied, diverging from the documented intent of the branch and making the condition list impossible to reason about — smallest safe fix: make the arms mutually exclusive (e.g. change line 121's condition to `stress == -1 || stress == -0.5 && contains(primary)` and let line 124 own `stress == 0`), or add a comment documenting which arm is intended to win.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:472-611 — getNumber is a ~140-line god function with nested closures (appendLookup, extend_num) mutating captured `result` state, mixing currency/ordinal/year/decimal branches with duplicated `Int(word)`/`Decimal(n)` conversion and suffix-handling logic that already exists in stem_s/stem_ed/stem_ing — consequence: any fix to suffix handling or number-to-word conversion must be replicated in two places (getNumber's inline branches vs. the stem_* helpers), and the captured-state closures make the branch order load-bearing in ways tests can't pin down — smallest safe fix: extract the shared suffix dispatch (line 602-608) and the digit-to-word conversion into named helpers and have getNumber's branches call them, so the two copies can't diverge silently.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:351-429 — stem_s/stem_ed/stem_ing are three copies of the same shape (guard on count+suffix, try dropLast variants gated by isKnown, then lookup+post-process) that have already diverged in details: stem_s checks `word.count > 4` for "es"/"ies" but stem_ed uses `word.count > 4` for "ed" while stem_ing uses `word.count > 5` for "ing" and a separate `word.count > 5` for the doubled-regex branch — consequence: a bug fix to the shared morphology (e.g. the isKnown gating or the dropLast counts) must be applied three times and will drift, as the differing count thresholds already show — smallest safe fix: factor the common "try candidate stems in priority order, first isKnown hit wins" loop into one helper parameterized by suffix list and stem-rewriter, and keep only the divergent post-processing (pluralizeS/pastEd/progIng) local.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:368-383 — pluralizeS and pastEd both encode the same "sibilant/stop → append s/z or t/d" morphology with overlapping character-class literals ("ptkfθ" vs "pkfθʃsʧ", "szʃʒʧʤ" vs the british-ɪ branch) that are not shared constants — consequence: the two magic character sets are near-duplicates that will diverge when one is corrected (e.g. adding ʧ to the plural set but forgetting the past-tense set), producing inconsistent plural vs. past-tense phonetics for the same stem — smallest safe fix: hoist the shared consonant-class Sets to file-scope constants next to the vocab Sets (lines 19-34) and reference them from both helpers.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:213-266 — getSpecialCase is a 50-line god function whose arms each re-derive the same "is this the article/preposition/pronoun X in context" question with slightly different tag/stress/ctx predicates (e.g. "am" checks `ctx.futureVowel == nil || word != "am" || stress! > 0` while "an" checks only `word == "AN"` and "the" ignores tag entirely) — consequence: adding a new special-case word requires choosing among four incompatible predicate styles, and the divergence is already visible in that "TO" (line 244) accepts tag==.preposition but "IN" (line 254) requires `!(tag?.isProperNoun ?? false)` — smallest safe fix: extract each word's handling into a small named case (or a dictionary of closures) so the predicate style is uniform and reviewable per word.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:271-300 — lookup mutates its `word` parameter and threads `isNNP` through three optional states (nil / false / true) where `isNNP != true` at line 280 conflates "not a proper noun" with "undetermined", so the silvers fallback (line 281-283) fires for undetermined-as-well-as-non-NNP words — consequence: a word whose NNP status was never resolved can be answered from the silver dictionary with rating 3 even when the gold dictionary miss was due to case, silently degrading the rating for a lookup the caller expected to be gold-or-nothing — smallest safe fix: initialize `isNNP` to `false` (not nil) and set it true only in the uppercased branch, so the `!= true` test means exactly "not NNP".
- [low] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:333-349 — isKnown's final block (lines 345-348) re-derives case information via index arithmetic (`word.index(after:)`, `word[idx...].uppercased() == word[idx...]`) that duplicates the simpler `word == word.uppercased()` / `golds[word.lowercased()]` checks already used at line 346, and the index-based tail can crash on single-character strings whose `index(after: startIndex)` is endIndex-adjacent only when `word.count == 1` didn't already return — consequence: the duplicated case logic is one more place for an off-by-one if the count==1 early return is ever relaxed, and readers must trace String.Index arithmetic to learn it's just "rest of word is lowercase" — smallest safe fix: replace lines 347-348 with `word.dropFirst().uppercased() == word.dropFirst()` (or an equivalent allSatisfy isLowercase check) so no index arithmetic is needed.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:431-437 — isCurrency's fallback chain resolves permissive: an input with no "." returns true unconditionally, and a cents part of exactly "0" (Set(cents) == Set(["0"])) also returns true, so malformed currency strings like "5." or "0.0" pass the currency gate and reach the currency-conversion branch of getNumber — consequence: a token like "5." is treated as a valid dollar amount and phonemized through the currency path instead of falling through to the plain-number path, producing wrong audio for edge-case inputs — smallest safe fix: require the cents part to be non-empty and all-zero-digits via `cents.allSatisfy { $0 == "0" } && !cents.isEmpty` rather than the Set-equality shortcut, and return false when the split yields no cents component.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:451-465 — isNumber's suffix loop breaks after the first matching suffix (line 458-459 `break`), so a word like "singing" matches "ing" first and never tries the shorter suffixes, and the loop's `core` is then tested with `allSatisfy` on characters that may include the stripped suffix's letters — consequence: numbers with multiple suffix-like tails (e.g. "2ing" vs "2'ing") can be misclassified depending on suffix order in the literal array at line 453, an ordering-sensitive behavior that is invisible at the call site — smallest safe fix: iterate suffixes longest-first (sort by count descending) before the loop, or drop the `break` and keep stripping until no suffix matches, so classification no longer depends on array literal order.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:148-150 — transcribe derives `stress` from `word == word.lowercased()` / `word == word.uppercased()` after line 148 has already replaced every numeric character via `unicodeNumericIfNeeded`, but the capStresses tuple (line 37) is typed `(Double, Double)` and used as `capStresses.1`/`capStresses.0` with no named labels — consequence: the 0.5/2.0 magic values are positionally indexed with no way to tell which is "capitalized" vs "all-caps" without reading the tuple declaration, and a swap of the tuple elements would silently invert the stress mapping for capitalized vs. shouted words — smallest safe fix: replace the unlabeled tuple with two named constants (`static let capStress = 0.5; static let upperStress = 2.0`) or a labeled tuple `(cap: Double, upper: Double)` used with `.cap`/`.upper` at the call sites.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:19-20 — usVocab/gbVocab are built from raw string literals whose character sets differ only in a handful of glyphs (us has "bdfhj…vwzæðŋɑɔ…", gb has "QWY…ɒː…"), with no comment or test pinning which characters are intentionally present in each dialect — consequence: a typo in either literal (e.g. dropping ə from one) silently changes which phonetic glyphs are treated as vowels for US vs GB, and the divergence is undiscoverable without diffing the two 60+-char strings by eye — smallest safe fix: derive gbVocab from usVocab plus/minus an explicit small delta Set (e.g. `gbVocab = usVocab.union(gbOnly).subtracting(usOnly)`) so the intentional differences are named, or add a unit test asserting the exact expected delta between the two Sets.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:30-34 — currencies dictionary values are unlabeled tuples `(String, String)` consumed positionally as `units.0`/`units.1` at lines 555-573 — consequence: "dollar/cent", "pound/pence", "euro/cent" are only distinguishable by remembering that .0 is major and .1 is minor; adding a currency with the pair reversed would silently swap major/minit phonetics — smallest safe fix: use a labeled tuple type `(major: String, minor: String)` for the dictionary's value type and update the two consumption sites to `units.major`/`units.minor`.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:555-574 — the currency branch of getNumber builds `pairs` then filters with `.filter { _ in true }` (line 560), a no-op filter that suggests an intended predicate was lost — consequence: the filter is dead code that misleads readers into thinking some pairs are being dropped, and if the intended predicate (e.g. dropping zero-valued pairs) is restored later it will conflict with the adjacent zero-handling at lines 561-564 — smallest safe fix: delete the `.filter { _ in true }` call and assign `pairs` directly from the two-element array literal.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:534 — `lookup("O", tag: nil, stress: -2, ctx: nil) as! (String, Int)` force-casts the lookup result — consequence: if lookup's return type ever changes (it is currently `(phoneme: String?, rating: Int?)`), this `as!` cast traps at runtime on the phonemization hot path, and the cast also silently discards the optionality that every other call site handles with `if let` — smallest safe fix: remove the `as!` and destructure with `if let (p, r) = lookup(...), let p, let r { result.append((p, r)) }` matching the appendLookup helper's pattern.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:101-110 — restress builds `indexedChars` as `[(Double, Character)]` where the Double is overloaded to mean both "original index" and "adjusted position (index - 0.5)", then sorts by that Double — consequence: the tuple's first element has two incompatible meanings within one function, and the sort at line 110 depends on the -0.5 offset interacting correctly with integer indices; any future adjustment (e.g. a different stress offset) breaks the ordering silently — smallest safe fix: use two distinct fields in the tuple (e.g. `(position: Double, char: Character)` with a comment that position starts as the index and is rewritten by the stress loop) or a small struct so the dual meaning is explicit.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:143-146 — transcribe normalizes curly quotes (8216/8217) but not the double-prime/low-quote variants (8220/8221, 8223, 8257/8258) that precomposedStringWithCompatibilityMapping does not fold to ASCII apostrophe — consequence: tokens containing U+201C/U+201D-style quotes bypass the alias normalization and are treated as unknown letters in getWord/isKnown, producing nil phonemes for words the curly-single-quote path already handles — smallest safe fix: extend the replacement chain (or use a single CharacterSet-based transform) to cover the remaining quote-like scalars so all apostrophe-equivalents reach the dictionary as "'".
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:189 — the getWord fast-path condition at line 183-189 is a single 7-clause `if` with `contains(where:)` closures over `[stem_s, stem_ed, stem_ing]` (line 189) that invoke the full stem functions just to decide whether to enter the slow path — consequence: the predicate re-runs stem_s/stem_ed/stem_ing (each of which calls lookup and the dictionary) purely as a boolean test, then the slow path re-runs them again at lines 201-208, doubling dictionary work on the hot phonemization path for every unknown word — smallest safe fix: drop the stem-function probe from the condition (the slow path already handles the nil case by returning (nil, nil)) or cache the stem results from the probe and reuse them in lines 201-208.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:9-11 — the three compiled NSRegularExpression patterns are file-scope `try!` initializers — consequence: a malformed pattern (e.g. the doubledIngRegex's `([bcdgklmnprstvxz])\1ing$` backreference) would crash at load rather than being caught by an error path, and `try!` on the hot-path statics means any future pattern edit is a load-time crash risk with no test coverage of the regexes themselves — smallest safe fix: wrap the three invariants in a unit test that constructs each regex (or switch to a non-throwing literal-pattern API) so a bad pattern fails in CI instead of at app launch.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:24-28 — addSymbols/symbolSet are two parallel dictionaries mapping punctuation to words ("."→"dot", "/"→"slash" vs "%→percent", "&→and", "+→plus", "@→at") with no shared key set or test — consequence: a symbol added to one dictionary but not the other (e.g. "/" missing from symbolSet) produces inconsistent handling between the tag==.punctuation branch (line 214) and the generic symbol branch (line 216), and nothing flags the asymmetry — smallest safe fix: merge into one dictionary keyed by symbol with a `kind` field (punctuation vs. symbol), or add a test asserting the two key sets' relationship.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:22-23 — ordinals is a Set of 4 strings while lexiconOrdinals is a 39-element Int range list built by concatenating Array(65...90) and Array(97...122) with two magic seeds (39, 45) — consequence: the two ordinal representations must stay in sync (a new ordinal suffix like "e" would need both updated), and the seeds 39/45 have no comment explaining they are "'" (39) and "-" (45) — smallest safe fix: replace the magic seeds with character literals (`Int(Character("'").unicodeScalars.first!.value)` or simply `[39, 45]` commented as apostrophe/hyphen) and derive lexiconOrdinals from a CharacterSet so the two lists share one source of truth.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:472-611 — getNumber's `extend_num` closure captures `result` and `first`-style flags across ~120 lines and ~10 branches, with `result.removeLast()` (line 501) mutating the shared array inside a nested closure — consequence: the function's behavior depends on branch-entry order in ways that are untestable without reproducing the whole state machine; a refactor that reorders two branches changes output with no compile-time signal — smallest safe fix: convert `result` from a captured var into an explicit accumulator parameter passed to each helper (or return values from extend_num) so the mutation points are visible at each call site.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:59-76 — growDictionary's merge uses `e.merging(d) { (_, original) in original }` where the closure ignores the incoming `e` value and always keeps `d`'s — consequence: the comment says "giving priority to original", but the closure's parameter naming (`(_, original)`) makes it ambiguous which dictionary is "original"; since `e` is the newly-grown variants and `d` is the source, the merge silently prefers the source over the grown variants whenever keys collide, which is the opposite of what "grow" implies for a key that exists in both — smallest safe fix: rename the closure parameters to `(grown, source)` and keep the source-priority explicit with a comment, or invert to `{ grown, _ in grown }` if grown-variants should win, so the intent is unambiguous at the merge site.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:41-43 — golds/silvers are typed `[String: Any]` and every consumer must cast (`as? String`, `as? [String: String?]`, `as? (String, Int)`-style patterns at lines 232, 263, 265, 285) — consequence: the Any-typed dictionaries push all shape knowledge to cast sites scattered across getSpecialCase/lookup/getNNP, so a resource-format change (e.g. silver entries becoming [String: String] instead of String) compiles cleanly and silently returns nil at every cast site — smallest safe fix: type golds/silvers as an enum-wrappered entry type (e.g. `enum DictEntry { case phoneme(String); case table([String: String?]) }`) or split into two typed dictionaries so the casts collapse into one exhaustive switch.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:313-331 — getNNP's `pieces` uses `compactMap` returning `[String?]` (line 314) and then tests `pieces.contains(where: { $0 == nil })` (line 322) — consequence: the compactMap's closure returns `nil` for non-letters but the joined output at line 324 uses `pieces.compactMap { $0 }`, so the nil-detection at line 322 is the only thing distinguishing "letter with no dictionary entry" from "non-letter"; the two paths are conflated in one array and a refactor of the closure's return type (e.g. returning "" instead of nil for non-letters) would silently break the all-letters-known check — smallest safe fix: separate the two signals by returning an enum or by tracking `unknownLetterCount` as an Int counter instead of encoding it as nils inside a compactMap result.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Lexicon/Lexicon.swift:302-310 — getParentTag maps pennTag prefixes to a second tag vocabulary ("VERB"/"NOUN"/"ADV"/"ADJ"/"XX") that is neither the NLTag input nor the PTB output of pennTag(for:) — consequence: the project now has three tag vocabularies (NLTag, PTB strings from PennTagUtil, and these VERB/NOUN/ADV/ADJ strings) with the mapping between the last two implicit in two files; a PTB tag added in PennTagUtil (e.g. "UH" or "FW") silently maps to "XX" here, changing lookup behavior for interjections/foreign words with no compile-time signal — smallest safe fix: have getParentTag consume the PTB string directly (it already receives the NLTag and calls pennTag) and document the PTB→parent-tag table in one place, or return the PTB tag itself and let callers switch on PTB prefixes.

"to"` (line 247), i.e. a dictionary miss silently degrades to the raw letters "to" as a phoneme — consequence: a missing or malformed gold entry for "to" produces the literal string "to" as phonetic output (letters, not phonemes), which downstream consumers will treat as valid phonetic text; the fallback direction is permissive (garbage-in accepted) rather than failing loudly — smallest safe fix: return nil (or log) when `golds["to"]` is nil in the futureVowel==nil branch so a dictionary miss is visible instead of silently phonemizing raw letters.

- [medium] supabase/migrations/20260314061409_initial_schema.sql:147-149 — storage bucket row inserted via raw `insert into storage.buckets` inside a migration — consequence: on a fresh Supabase project where the `storage.buckets` table/columns differ (or where the bucket already exists with different settings) the migration can fail or silently skip (`on conflict (id) do nothing` leaves an existing bucket with possibly non-public settings), making the recordings bucket config diverge between environments — smallest safe fix: create the bucket via the storage API/extension's supported procedure or guard with explicit column checks, and drop the `do nothing` so divergence is surfaced.
- [medium] supabase/migrations/20260314061409_initial_schema.sql:151-163 — storage policies named "Cast members can upload/read recordings" actually grant any authenticated user upload/read on the whole bucket — consequence: any authenticated user can upload arbitrary files into the recordings bucket and read every other production's audio, since the checks only test `bucket_id` and `auth.role()`, not cast membership or folder ownership — smallest safe fix: add an `exists (...)` cast-membership/production-ownership predicate (or per-user folder prefix check) to both policies, and rename them to match behavior.
- [medium] supabase/migrations/20260314061409_initial_schema.sql:165-170 — update policy on storage.objects checks only `auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]` with no bucket_id predicate — consequence: an authenticated user can update objects in any bucket whose first folder segment equals their uid (e.g. a future bucket using the same layout), and the policy name "Users can update own recordings" overstates the guard — smallest safe fix: add `bucket_id = 'recordings'` to the using clause.
- [low] supabase/migrations/20260314061409_initial_schema.sql:106-135 — recordings table has no organizer-write policy, only user-owned insert/update — consequence: the production organizer cannot manage recordings uploaded by cast members (e.g. delete a bad take), an operational gap rather than a security hole — smallest safe fix: add an organizer-scoped policy if organizer management is intended, or document the limitation.
- [medium] supabase/migrations/20260314061409_initial_schema.sql:71-79 — cast_members select policy uses a self-referential `exists` on the same table without a distinct row guard — consequence: the policy evaluates per-row and can permit reads of rows the user did not create when another row in the same production matches (intended), but the subquery lacks `cm.id = cast_members.id`-style scoping so it relies solely on the production match; combined with the deferred productions policy at :92-100 this creates a circular dependency (cast_members policy depends on productions, productions policy depends on cast_members) that can break RLS evaluation order on fresh databases — smallest safe fix: verify policy evaluation with a bootstrap path (e.g. allow organizer select on cast_members via productions join) and add a comment/test pinning the dependency order.

- [medium] lib/data/services/perf_service.dart:25-32 — `measure` starts a trace but if `operation()` throws the finally stops the trace and the exception propagates — fine — but the real defect: `startTrace` swallows all exceptions with `catch (_)` returning null, so a misconfigured Firebase Performance (e.g. missing `FirebasePerformance.instance` on unsupported platforms) silently disables every measurement with no log — consequence: perf regressions ship unnoticed because the wrapper never reports why traces are absent — smallest safe fix: log the caught error via `DebugLogService.instance.logError(LogCategory.error, 'startTrace failed', e)` before returning null.
- [low] lib/data/services/perf_service.dart:10-11 — `_perf` getter re-evaluates `firebaseAvailable` on every call and constructs `FirebasePerformance.instance` fresh each time; if `firebaseAvailable` is a cheap const this is fine, but the getter is called per trace with no memoization — consequence: repeated platform checks per trace start, minor overhead in hot paths — smallest safe fix: cache the resolved instance in a nullable field computed once.
- [medium] lib/data/services/perf_service.dart:14-22 — `startTrace` returns `Trace?` but callers of `measure` cannot distinguish "trace started" from "trace unavailable"; the doc comment says "Call [Trace.stop] when the operation completes" yet `measure` is the only in-file caller and handles stop itself — consequence: public surface larger than its use; external callers must replicate the try/finally pattern — smallest safe fix: make `startTrace` private (`_startTrace`) unless an external caller exists (assumed none in this batch).
- [low] lib/data/services/playback_session.dart:26-35 — `ensurePlayback` catches all exceptions and only logs via `DebugLogService.instance.logError` with `LogCategory.error`; the catch parameter is typed `catch (e)` (non-`_`), fine, but the failure mode is silent-to-user: playback proceeds with a possibly still-`.record` category, producing the exact "no audible output" bug the doc describes — consequence: recordings sound empty with no user-visible signal beyond a debug log line — smallest safe fix: surface the failure to the caller (return a bool or rethrow after logging) so the play path can warn.
- [low] lib/data/services/playback_session.dart:27 — platform guard `!Platform.isIOS && !Platform.isAndroid` returns silently on desktop/web; doc says "No-op on desktop" so this is intended, but web (`kIsWeb`) is neither iOS nor Android and `Platform.isIOS` throws on web in some Flutter versions — consequence: potential runtime exception on web builds before the try/catch — smallest safe fix: add `if (kIsWeb) return;` guard first (assumed web is a target; if not, no change needed).

- [medium] lib/data/services/recording_sync_service.dart:436-437 — `cachePath` is called with `productionId`/`lineId` from cloud rows; `cachePath` validates via `isSafePathId` and throws on hostile ids, but the download loop's catch (454-458) swallows the `ArgumentError` as a generic download failure — consequence: a poisoned row is logged as "download failed" rather than the diagnosable unsafe-id message the boundary comment promises — smallest safe fix: check `isSafePathId` before the try (as the realtime path does at 619-623) and log the specific unsafe-id error.
- [medium] lib/data/services/recording_sync_service.dart:626 — realtime handler skips payloads where `recordUserId == (myUserId ?? _cloud.currentUserId)`; when both are null (anonymous), `recordUserId` of `null` equals the null RHS and *every* payload with no `user_id` is silently dropped — consequence: castmate recordings with a missing user_id are never downloaded in anonymous sessions — smallest safe fix: compare only when the resolved user id is non-null (`final me = myUserId ?? _cloud.currentUserId; if (me != null && recordUserId == me) return;`).

- [medium] lib/data/services/script_export.dart:243-262 — `toCueScript` iterates all dialogue lines and, for a matching character, prints the *previous* dialogue line as the cue regardless of which character spoke it; for a character's first line at index 0 no cue is printed (correct), but for consecutive lines by the same character the same cue line is repeated — consequence: duplicated cue lines in the exported cue script — smallest safe fix: track the last emitted cue line index and skip repeats.

- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:470 — `2 << nextRetry.retryCount.clamp(0, 4)` computes the backoff delay from the retry count of the FIRST failed job only, and the shift is applied to the literal 2 rather than a named constant — consequence: all failed jobs retry on the same timer regardless of their individual retryCount, and the magic `2`/`5`/`30` constants are duplicated between the retry path (line 470), the not-ready path (line 363), and the gave-up threshold (line 421) with no single source of truth — fix: compute per-job delay inside the timer callback (or store retryCount on the timer) and hoist `2`/`5`/`30` into named constants.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:249 — `queuedKeys.add(key)` mutates the set while iterating `restored`, so a restored job whose key was already added by an earlier restored job is silently dropped even though the live queue never contained it — consequence: a duplicate persisted job (e.g. from a crash between enqueue and persist) is dropped from restore without any log, and the "restored N" count under-reports what was actually kept — fix: check membership with `queuedKeys.contains(key)` before adding, and log the dropped duplicate.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:243-244 — the dedup key `'${productionId}/${lineId}'` is built by string concatenation with no escaping, so a production id containing `/` or a line id containing `/` collides with a different (productionId, lineId) pair — consequence: two distinct jobs can be treated as the same line during restore dedup and during enqueue's `sameLine` check (line 318-319), silently replacing the wrong job — fix: use a tuple/record key or join with a separator that cannot appear in the ids (e.g. `\u0000`).
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:325 — job id `'${productionId}_${lineId}_${ms}'` is not guaranteed unique: two enqueues for the same line within the same millisecond (or a line id containing `_` colliding with a different production/line pair) produce identical ids — consequence: `fromJson`/`toJson` round-trips and any future id-based lookup cannot distinguish the jobs; the current code never looks up by id so the blast radius is latent, but the id is persisted to disk and exported in logs — fix: add a monotonically increasing counter or UUID to the id.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:388 — `file.lengthSync()` is called on the UI isolate inside the upload loop; for a large recording this blocks the event loop for the whole stat — consequence: a multi-MB file on a slow network volume (or a hung FUSE/NFS mount) freezes the UI/rehearsal loop while the queue is processing — fix: use `await file.length()` (async) or `file.stat()` instead of the sync variant.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:379 — `file.existsSync()` is likewise a synchronous disk probe on the hot upload path (and again at line 247 during restore) — consequence: same UI-thread stall class as the lengthSync above; on a cold start with many restored jobs the restore loop does N synchronous existsSync calls before the first frame — fix: switch to `await file.exists()` in the async paths; for restore, batch the probes off the UI isolate.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:216 — `jsonDecode(await file.readAsString())` is typed `dynamic` and the corrupt-file guard only catches a `FormatException`; a file containing valid JSON of the wrong shape (e.g. a top-level List) passes the try, then hits `if (data is! Map) return;` at line 228 which silently discards every queued job without moving the file aside or logging — consequence: a structurally-valid-but-wrong queue file destroys all pending uploads on the next persist (the empty in-memory queue overwrites it), the exact loss the comment at 186-189 says the tmp+rename was meant to prevent — fix: treat a non-Map payload the same as a corrupt file: log, rename to `.corrupt`, and return before any persist can clobber it.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:230-237 — `data['pending'] as List? ?? []` and `data['failed'] as List? ?? - [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:66-68 — `DateTime.tryParse(json['createdAt'] as String? ?? '') ?? DateTime.now()` fabricates a fresh timestamp when the persisted field is missing or unparseable — consequence: a restored job's `recordedAt`/freshness comparison (the field the doc comment at 23-24 says is used for cross-device freshness) silently becomes "now", making a stale recording look fresh on other devices; the fallback resolves to the riskier value — fix: drop the job (or keep it with a logged warning) when createdAt cannot be parsed, rather than substituting `DateTime.now()`.

- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:114 — `supa.currentUser!.id` uses a bang on a nullable field inside `saveMetadata` — consequence: if the user signed out between `upload()` and `saveMetadata()` (offline sign-out, token revocation), the null assertion throws inside the persist path and the job is treated as failed/retried forever with a crash-shaped error rather than a clean retry — fix: guard with `final user = supa.currentUser; if (user == null) throw ...` or pass the user id captured before the upload.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:132-135 — `SyncQueue.forTesting(this._uploader, {String? persistPath})` sets `_persistToDisk = persistPath != null` but leaves `_persistPathOverride` nullable; when `persistPath` is null the constructor still runs the default `_persistPath()` (line 159-163) which calls `getApplicationSupportDirectory()` — consequence: a test that passes no path silently hits the real platform directory plugin, which throws in unit-test environments (or writes into the developer's actual app-support dir), a test-only footgun — fix: require `persistPath` in the testing constructor or make `_persistPath()` throw when `_persistToDisk` is true but no override and no platform dir is available.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:285-296 — `start()` subscribes to connectivity and kicks `_processQueue()` but never cancels/re-creates the retry timer if `start()` is called twice (e.g. hot-restart or a second screen entering rehearsal) — consequence: two connectivity subscriptions and two 30s retry timers can coexist (the second `start()` cancels only `_connectivitySub`, not `_retryTimer`), doubling upload attempts and racing `_processing` — fix: make `start()` idempotent (early-return if already started) or cancel `_retryTimer` alongside the subscription.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:299-304 — `stop()` cancels the connectivity sub and retry timer but leaves `_processing` true if it is called mid-upload — consequence: a subsequent `enqueue()` (line 342 `if (!_processing) _processQueue()`) sees `_processing == true` and never kicks the queue; the job sits pending until the next connectivity event — fix: reset `_processing = false` in `stop()` (or guard the flag reset in `_processQueue`'s finally).
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:350-351 — `_processQueue` early-returns when `_pending.isEmpty` but the `_processing` flag is never cleared on that path if a previous run left it true — consequence: after `stop()` mid-upload (see above) or an exception escaping the while-loop body, `_processing` stays true and every future `enqueue`/connectivity kick is a no-op; the queue is permanently stalled until app restart — fix: wrap the body in try/finally that resets `_processing`, or re-check the flag at the top of `_processQueue`.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:462-465 — after the loop, `if (_pending.isNotEmpty) { scheduleMicrotask(_processQueue); return; }` re-enters `_processQueue` via microtask, but `_processing` was already set to false at line 457 — consequence: two `_processQueue` invocations can overlap if a connectivity event fires between the flag reset and the microtask, since the guard at line 351 only checks `_processing` at entry and the microtask path bypasses the flag — fix: keep `_processing == true` across the microtask hand-off and clear it only when the queue is truly drained.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:476-480 — the retry timer callback moves ALL failed jobs back to pending and clears `_failed` unconditionally, even if the uploader is still not ready — consequence: `_processQueue` then hits the not-ready branch (line 354), logs "will retry in 30s", and the failed jobs sit in `_pending` while `_failed` is empty, so the backoff state (retryCount-driven delay) is lost and the next failure restarts the delay from the job's current retryCount rather than the accumulated backoff — fix: only promote failed jobs when `_uploader.isReady`, or keep them in `_failed` until ready.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:419 — `job.retryCount++` mutates the job after `_persist()` has already been called at line 409 with the pre-increment count — consequence: the on-disk snapshot written by the persist at 409 records the old retryCount; if the process dies before the persist at 428, the retry budget is under-counted on restore (the job gets a fresh budget anyway per fromJson line 73, so the practical effect is a longer retry tail than intended) — fix: increment retryCount before the first persist in the failure branch.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:421 — the gave-up threshold is the literal `5` compared against `job.retryCount` which was just incremented, so the job gets exactly 5 attempts but the log at 425 says `(attempt ${job.retryCount}/5)` printing the already-incremented value — consequence: cosmetic off-by-one in the log (attempt 2/5 shown on the second attempt), which misleads anyone debugging retry exhaustion from logs — fix: log `job.retryCount` before incrementing, or use `attempt ${job.retryCount + 1}` consistently with line 392.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:435 — `onGaveUp?.call(job, e)` is invoked but the job is never removed from `_failed`/`_pending` nor persisted as removed — consequence: after gave-up, the job remains in `_failed` (it was never added there in this branch, but if it arrived via the retry-timer promotion at 477 it IS in `_pending` and stays there), so the next `_processQueue` pass re-enters the upload path for a job the callback was told was abandoned — fix: remove the job from all lists and persist before invoking `onGaveUp`.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:401 — `_persist()` is called after every successful upload and after every failure (lines 384, 401, 409, 428), each of which re-runs `_loadPersisted()` first (line 181) — consequence: every persist re-reads and re-parses the queue file from disk even though `_loaded` is true and the in-memory state is authoritative; with N jobs this is O(N) JSON decode per mutation, quadratic overall on a large queue — fix: skip the reload when `_loaded` is true (the restore is only needed before the first write), or cache the parsed snapshot.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:181 — `_loadPersisted()` is invoked inside `_serializedFileAccess` on EVERY persist, but `_loadPersisted` early-returns only when `_loaded` is true — after `reset()` (line 505) sets `_loaded = true`, a later `_persist()` still re-enters the try/catch and re-reads the file, and if the file was deleted by `reset()`'s persist the read silently succeeds on a stale cached path — consequence: wasted I/O per mutation and a stale-file read after clear — fix: gate the reload on `!_loaded` inside `_persist`'s action, not inside `_loadPersisted` alone.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:191-193 — `File('$path.tmp')` is written and renamed, but if two processes (or a previous crashed run's tmp file) exist, `rename` on some platforms fails when the destination exists and the tmp file is left behind — consequence: orphaned `.tmp` files accumulate in the app-support directory and are never cleaned; on platforms where rename-over-existing is not atomic the persist can throw and the queue silently stops persisting (the catch at 194 only logs) — fix: delete the tmp file in a `finally`/catch, and use `rename` with an existing-destination-safe strategy (delete-then-rename or copy+fsync).

- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:288 — `results.any((r) => r != ConnectivityResult.none)` treats a `ConnectivityResult` list as "has connection" without checking whether the network can actually reach the internet (e.g. captive portal, VPN with no route) — consequence: the queue kicks `_processQueue` on a useless connection, burns an upload attempt, increments retryCount, and burns retry budget on every captive-portal re-check — fix: gate the kick on a reachability check (or let the upload failure path handle it without incrementing retryCount for network-unavailable errors).

- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:363 — `Timer(const Duration(seconds: 30), _processQueue)` passes the method tear-off directly; if `_processQueue` throws (e.g. the uploader throws synchronously before the try), the timer callback error is unhandled and the zone crashes — consequence: an unhandled async error in a timer callback can take down the isolate in release builds — fix: wrap the callback body (`() { _processQueue(); }` with a try/catch) or ensure `_processQueue` cannot throw synchronously.
- [medium] lib/data/services/sync_queue.dart:477 — `_pending.addAll(_failed); _failed.clear();` runs inside the timer callback without re-checking `_processing` — consequence: if `_processQueue` is already running (kicked by connectivity), the timer callback mutates `_pending`/`_failed` concurrently with the loop's `remove`/`add` operations, which can duplicate a job in `_pending` (the loop's `continue` paths leave the job in `_pending` while the timer also re-adds it) — fix: guard the timer callback with `if (!_processing)` or route the promotion through the same serialized entry point.

- [medium] lib/data/services/wav_silence.dart:31-48 — `_parse`'s chunk-walk and `_frameSize`'s chunk-walk (104-117) are the same loop duplicated with diverged behavior — the parser stops at the first `data` chunk while `_frameSize` keeps walking and can return a frame size from a *later* `fmt ` chunk (or the fallback 2) even when `_parse` already validated the header — consequence: a multi-chunk WAV (e.g. LIST/LABEL chunks after `fmt `) gets silence padded using a frame size derived from a different chunk than the one `_parse` used, misaligning the pad to whole frames and corrupting sample alignment — smallest safe fix: have `prepend`/`_parse` return the frame size (or the fmt chunk offset) in `_WavInfo` and delete the second walk in `_frameSize`.
- [medium] lib/data/services/wav_silence.dart:76-79 — `padBytes` is computed from `byteRate` (bytes per *second*) multiplied by milliseconds/1000, but `byteRate` is bytes per second of *all* channels; the comment at 103 says frame = channels × bits/8, so rounding `padBytes % frameSize` can round the pad *down* below one frame when byteRate/frameSize is small — consequence: `padBytes -= padBytes % frameSize` can floor to 0 after the subtraction even though `padBytes > 0` above, silently returning `source` (no silence prepended) for low-rate mono files the function was written for — smallest safe fix: compute `padBytes = frameSize * ((byteRate * ms/1000) ~/ frameSize)` and only bail when that is ≤ 0, or document the floor-to-frame as intentional.
- [low] lib/data/services/wav_silence.dart:98-100 — `catch (_)` swallows every failure mode (unreadable source, unwritable destination, OOM on a huge WAV) and returns `source` — consequence: a caller that checks the returned path cannot distinguish "no silence needed" from "prepend failed and destination was never written", and the exception detail is discarded — smallest safe fix: catch narrower exceptions (FileSystemException) or log/rethrow after returning `source` so the failure is observable.
- [low] lib/data/services/wav_silence.dart:118 — comment claims "16-bit mono, which is what Kokoro emits" as the fallback for `_frameSize`, but the loop above can already return a frame from any `fmt ` chunk; the fallback silently assumes a format the caller never verified — consequence: a WAV whose `fmt ` chunk appears after `data` (legal but unusual) gets a hardcoded 2-byte frame used to align the pad — smallest safe fix: derive the fallback from the parsed `fmt ` fields captured in `_WavInfo` instead of a literal 2.
