- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:335-417 — `detectBoxes` is a god function with 5-deep nesting (seed loops → component loop → neighbor pushes → visited/threshold checks) and inlined flood-fill — the 4 neighbor blocks at 369-400 are four copies of the same 6-line push sequence differing only in the offset — smallest safe fix: extract a `pushNeighbor(stack, visited, prob, np, detThresh)` helper and collapse the four blocks.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:342-343 — `visited = BooleanArray(mW * mH)` and `stack = IntArray(4096)` are allocated per `detectBoxes` call — for a 960×1280 detection tensor that's a 1.2MB BooleanArray plus stack churn per page, re-allocated every call — smallest safe fix: hoist to reusable instance fields cleared per call, or size the stack from `mW*mH` upper bound once.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:408 — `dist` uses `detUnclipRatio` (0.4) directly in the unclip formula `area·ratio/perimeter` — PP-OCR's unclip expands by `area·k/perimeter` with k≈0.4 as a *ratio of the expanded box*, and the Swift twin (per the header comment) validated this on Mac; but here the same constant is applied to the *shrunken* component bounds rather than the recovered box, so dense multi-line pages get systematically tighter crops — smallest safe fix: verify against the Swift plugin's exact unclip geometry and align the formula, not just the constant.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:409-412 — `x0/y0/x1/y1` scale the *unclipped* component bounds by `sx/sy` (orig/det ratio) but clamp `minX - dist - 1` against 0 and `maxX + dist + 2` against `mW` in *detection* coords before scaling — the `+2` slack is in det pixels, so at scale 3× (1800px render → 960px det) the unclip margin is effectively 0.67 orig-px, diverging from the Swift plugin's geometry — smallest safe fix: apply the ±dist slack after scaling, or scale dist by `1/sx` first.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:419-426 — `cropBitmap` clamps `box.right` to `src.width` but never clamps `box.left` below `src.width` or `box.right` below 0 — a box with `left > src.width` yields `w = min(src.width, right) - left` which can be negative and returns null (safe), but a box with `right < 0` yields `w = 0 - x` ≤ 0 → null (safe) — actually safe; however `box.top`/`bottom` are never clamped against each other, so an inverted box (top > bottom) silently produces `h ≤ 0` → null and the line is dropped with no log — smallest safe fix: log dropped boxes so silent OCR loss is diagnosable.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:429-465 — `recognize` returns `null` for a zero-height crop (432) but the caller at 312 does `?: continue` — combined with `cropBitmap` returning null at 424, three distinct failure modes (no crop, no run, empty text) all collapse to "skip silently" with no counter — a page whose every box fails recognition reports `lines: []` indistinguishable from a blank page — smallest safe fix: count skipped boxes and include in the per-page log line.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:440 — `if (shape.size != 3) return null` — the rec model's output rank is asserted at runtime per crop; if the ONNX export changes rank (e.g. batch dim folded), every crop silently returns null and all pages report empty lines with only a per-crop null, no log — smallest safe fix: log a single warning on first rank mismatch instead of per-crop silent null.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:457 — `if (idx < keys.size) sb.append(keys[idx]) else sb.append(' ')` — an out-of-range CTC index silently becomes a space instead of surfacing a dictionary/model mismatch — a rec model exported with a different vocab than `keys.txt` produces plausible-looking garbage text with no error — smallest safe fix: log once on the first out-of-range index and treat it as a model/asset mismatch.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:463 — `conf = probSum / emitted` averages only *emitted* timesteps' probabilities, ignoring blanks — this diverges from PP-OCR's per-line confidence (which averages over all decoded frames including collapse) and inflates confidence on sparse lines — smallest safe fix: align with the Swift plugin's confidence definition or document the divergence.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:470-488 — `imageToTensor` recycles `scaled` in `finally` only when `scaled !== src`, but when `src.width == w && src.height == h` the branch reuses `src` — safe here — however `Bitmap.createScaledBitmap` can return the *same* instance when dimensions match even in the else branch, making `scaled === src` and skipping recycle (correct) — no leak; but the `getPixels` path on a recycled-then-reused bitmap would throw — currently safe, no finding beyond noting the fragile invariant — smallest safe fix: none needed; skip.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:491-504 — `run()` returns `null` on missing `env` or non-tensor first output with no logging — a session whose output ordering changed (results[0] not the tensor) silently nulls every call and the whole OCR pipeline reports empty — smallest safe fix: log the output names/types once at load and assert the expected tensor is present.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:493 — `session.inputNames.firstOrNull() ?: "x"` — falling back to the literal name "x" when the session reports no inputs is a permissive fallback that masks a broken model — smallest safe fix: return null (or throw) when `inputNames` is empty rather than guessing "x".
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:64-71 — `onAttachedToEngine` starts the model-load thread unconditionally with no guard against a second attach (Flutter re-attach on hot-restart can call it twice), and `loadModels` writes `detSession`/`recSession`/`keys`/`ready` from that thread with no synchronization beyond `@Volatile ready` — a second attach during a first load can produce two sessions, one leaked — smallest safe fix: guard with an AtomicBoolean compareAndSet on attach.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:73-81 — `onDetachedFromEngine` closes sessions from the main thread while `loadModels` may still be running on the worker (loading=true, ready=false) — the worker then assigns `detSession`/`recSession` after detach, leaking both open ONNX sessions and the `keys` list — smallest safe fix: join/cancel the load thread on detach, or have `loadModels` check a detached flag before assigning sessions.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:48-49 — `ready`/`loading` are `@Volatile` but `detSession`, `recSession`, `keys`, `env` are plain fields written by the worker thread and read by channel threads — without happens-before, a channel thread can see `ready == true` while `detSession` is still null (JMM allows reordering of the plain store vs the volatile store's visibility of *prior* plain stores only if the volatile write is after them — here `ready = true` at 106 is after the session assignments, so the volatile write does order them) — actually safe by JMM; but `env = e` at 105 is also before, fine — no finding; skip.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:97 — `threads = max(2, min(availableProcessors/2, 8))` — on a 2-core device this yields `max(2, min(1, 8)) = 2`, oversubscribing a 2-core phone with two sessions × 2 threads = 4 intra-op threads on 2 cores — smallest safe fix: cap at `availableProcessors` not `availableProcessors/2` floor of 2, e.g. `max(1, min(cores/2, 8))` with cores≥4 fast path.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:99 — `opts.addConfigEntry("session.intra_op.allow_spinning", "0")` — a magic string config key with no constant and no comment linking to ORT docs; if ORT renames/ignores it the setting silently no-ops — smallest safe fix: reference the ORT constant or log whether the config entry was accepted.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:103-104 — `keys = String(...).split("\n").dropLastWhile { it.isEmpty() }` — splits only on `\n`, so a CRLF dictionary leaves `\r` on every key, shifting every index by one character and corrupting all recognized text — smallest safe fix: split on `\r?\n` or trim each entry.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:282-283 — `lastDetMs`/`lastRecMs` are instance fields mutated from worker threads and read in the log at 239 with no synchronization — on a multi-page PDF the log line can interleave det/rec timings across pages, misattributing timings — smallest safe fix: make them local per-page values returned alongside the lines, or `@Volatile`.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:292 — `ratio = min(detLimitSide/longSide, 1.0f)` — when the bitmap's long side is *smaller* than 960 the ratio is 1.0 and the det tensor is the full bitmap; but `renderPage` already scales the long side to ≈1800px, so det always sees ~960 — consistent; however for `recognizeText` on a raw image the det input can be up to 960 long side with no lower bound, so a 32px-wide image yields `newW = max(32, ...)` forcing upscale distortion — smallest safe fix: skip upscale when the source is already ≤32px or accept as-is.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:296 — `run(det, detIn, longArrayOf(1, 3, newH.toLong(), newW.toLong()))` — the det shape is hardcoded NCHW with batch 1 and 3 channels; if the exported det model expects NCHW with a *dynamic* H/W this is fine, but if it expects a fixed 960×960 the mismatch throws inside `run` → caught by `ocrImage`'s null path → silent empty result — smallest safe fix: log the ONNX exception in `run` before returning null so misconfiguration is diagnosable.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:296-297 — `run(...)` ?: return emptyList() — det failure and "no boxes found" both produce an empty list with no distinction — a model-load-time shape error would make every page look blank — smallest safe fix: have `run` log its exception (as above) so the two cases are distinguishable in logs.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:309 — `boxes.sortedBy { it.top }` sorts only by top, not by (top, left) — two boxes on the same line with different lefts get arbitrary relative order, scrambling reading order for multi-column lines — smallest safe fix: `sortedWith(compareBy({ it.top }, { it.left }))` with a row-tolerance grouping.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:317-322 — normalized rect uses `box.left / fOrigW` etc. where `fOrigW = max(origW, 1)` — for a 0-width bitmap (possible from a corrupt decode? decodeFile returns null then, so unreachable) — safe; skip.
- [medium] android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tiltastech/lineguide/PaddleOcrPlugin.kt:141 — `BitmapFactory.decodeFile(path)?.let { ocrImage(it) } ?: emptyList()` — the decoded bitmap is never recycled after `ocrImage` returns — for a large image this pins the full-resolution bitmap until GC; on a repeated-import loop this is the same fd/bitmap exhaustion class the Swift port fixed for PDFs — smallest safe fix: `val bmp = BitmapFactory.decodeFile(path); try { ocrImage(bmp) } finally { bmp?.recycle() }`.

scripts/play-changelog.sh — findings: 5
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:19-21 — version parsing assumes `version:` is the first pubspec key and splits on `+`/space with `${VAR#version: }`; a pubspec with comments/extra spaces or a `version: 1.2.3+4+5`-style line yields empty VERSION_CODE — consequence: changelog check at line 62 looks for `changelogs/.txt` and the AAB-staleness gate still passes while reporting the wrong versionCode to the operator — smallest safe fix: parse with `awk '/^version:/{print $2}'` and split major/minor/patch/code explicitly, failing loudly if empty.
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:29-33 — `STOREFILE` is taken verbatim from key.properties and used in `-f "android/app/$STOREFILE"`; a storeFile value containing `..` or an absolute path makes the check test a file outside android/app — consequence: preflight can report "release keystore present" for a path that is not the actual keystore (false pass) — smallest safe fix: reject values containing `/` or `..` before the `-f` test.
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:74 — alpha-channel probe shells out to python3/PIL with `|| echo 0` fallback; when PIL is missing the alpha check silently resolves to the permissive value (0 = no alpha) — consequence: an RGBA icon ships and Play rejects the upload after preflight said ready — smallest safe fix: treat missing PIL as a `bad` (or skip only when icon absent), not as "no alpha".
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:104-105 — `RATIO`/`TOO_TALL` computed via python3 with no fallback; if python3 is absent the loop's `bad` never fires and the aspect-ratio gate silently passes — consequence: oversized screenshots pass preflight and get rejected at upload — smallest safe fix: compute ratio with awk (`max(w/h,h/w)`) or fail the check when the helper is unavailable.
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:94-96 — `SHOTS=$(ls ... | wc -l | tr -d ' ' || true)` then `${SHOTS:-0}`; with zero screenshots `ls` fails and SHOTS becomes empty→0, but the `>= 2` branch at line 99 then reports "need at least 2" while line 96's `> 8` check is skipped for the empty case — consequence: consistent, but the `|| true` inside a `$( )` under `set -e` masks a real ls failure (e.g. dir unreadable) as "0 screenshots" — smallest safe fix: drop `|| true` and let the failure surface, or test `-d` first.
- [low] scripts/play-preflight.sh:117-121 — `bash -n "$sh" 2>/dev/null` then re-runs `bash -n "$sh" 2>&1 | head -1` for the message; two invocations can disagree (race/permission) and the first's stderr is discarded — consequence: a script that fails only under the second invocation reports a wrong/empty error line — smallest safe fix: capture output once: `err=$(bash -n "$sh" 2>&1)` and test `$?`.
- [low] scripts/play-preflight.sh:136 — `find ... -print -quit` stops at the first newer file, so the reported `$NEWER` is one arbitrary path; with many stale sources the operator sees a single file and may "fix" only that — consequence: repeated preflight passes after a partial rebuild — smallest safe fix: print count (`| wc -l`) plus first path, or list all.
- [low] scripts/play-preflight.sh:142 — `stat -f %z` is BSD-only; on GNU/Linux stat errors and `SIZE_MB` becomes empty under `set -e`/arith — consequence: script aborts at the size line on Linux hosts despite a valid AAB — smallest safe fix: use `wc -c < "$AAB"` or `du -m`.
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:22-24 — auto-detect takes `awk '{print $NF}'` of `xcrun devicectl` output; if the device line's last field is not the UDID (locale/columns change) UDID is garbage and the script proceeds — consequence: `idevicecrashreport -u <garbage>` fails silently (`|| true` at 48) and the script reports "No Runner crash logs found on device" — smallest safe fix: validate UDID against a regex (`^[0-9a-fA-F-]{8,}$`) before use.
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:48 — `idevicecrashreport ... || true` swallows every failure including "no device/permission denied"; combined with line 53's early `exit 0` the script reports success with no logs pulled — consequence: operator believes device had no crashes when the pull itself failed — smallest safe fix: distinguish "no .ips found" from "pull failed": check pull exit status and only `|| true` on expected no-device cases.
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:51 — `CRASHES` pipeline `while read f; do echo "$(basename "$f") $f"; done | sort -r | awk '{print $2}'` breaks on paths with spaces (basename is echoed first, so `$2` after sort is the basename, not the path) — consequence: `$LATEST` becomes a bare filename, python3 `open('$LATEST')` fails and the raw-header fallback at 137 also fails — smallest safe fix: keep full path only (`sort -r` on basename via `-t/ -k2` or prepend index) and pass `$LATEST` as argv to python3, not string-interpolated.
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:64-133 — the entire parser is one python3 -c heredoc with `$LATEST` interpolated into a quoted string; a path with `'` or `$()` breaks quoting and, worse, allows command substitution if the path contains backticks/`$(...)` — consequence: arbitrary shell execution from a crafted filename on the device (device-controlled input reaching a host shell) — smallest safe fix: pass the path via `sys.argv[1]` (`python3 -c '...' -- "$LATEST"`) and never interpolate into the code string.
- [high] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:67 — `open('$LATEST')` interpolates a device-derived filename into python source inside double-quoted shell string — consequence: a crash-log filename containing `'` or shell metacharacters (e.g. from a malicious/compromised device app) executes shell commands on the operator's Mac — smallest safe fix: pass path as argv (`python3 -c "..." "$LATEST"`) and read `sys.argv[1]`; same fix covers line 133's `print(f"Full crash log: $LATEST")`.
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:134-140 — fallback `head -5 "$LATEST"` / `grep -A5 ... "$LATEST"` runs even when the python block failed for a reason unrelated to file content (e.g. path with spaces per line 51) and `head`/`grep` on a nonexistent file print errors but the `|| { }` group succeeds — consequence: misleading "Raw crash header" output with no crash data, exit 0 — smallest safe fix: verify `[[ -f "$LATEST" ]]` before both branches.
- [low] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:13-14 — `CRASHDIR_LEGACY="/tmp/crashlogs"` is searched but never created; on a fresh host find on it is fine, but the legacy dir is a world-writable /tmp path — consequence: another local user can plant `Runner-*.ips` files that this script then parses and prints (info disclosure of fabricated crash content) — smallest safe fix: use a per-user dir (`$TMPDIR/$(id -u)-crashlogs`) or verify ownership before reading.
- [low] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:143-149 — `OTHER` lists up to 5 older crashes but the loop `while read f` re-runs basename on already-basename'd entries (from line 51's awk output) — consequence: harmless here since entries are bare names, but if line 51 is fixed to full paths this loop prints full paths twice-processed — smallest safe fix: after fixing line 51, use `basename` consistently or store name+path pairs.
- [low] scripts/play-preflight.sh:12 — `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."` with no quoting failure mode if path contains spaces is handled (`"$(dirname "$0")"` quoted) but `$0` may be a symlink; minor — no finding beyond noting it is fine. (suppressed)
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:46-59 — limits 31/81/4001 are off-by-one against the messages "≤ 30/≤ 80/≤ 4000": `> 31` allows a 31-char title while the message says ≤30 — consequence: preflight passes a title Play will reject — smallest safe fix: compare `> 30`, `> 80`, `> 4000` (or reword messages to `< 31`).
- [low] scripts/play-preflight.sh:85 — `stat -f %m` is BSD-only (GNU stat uses `-c %m` or `%Y`); on Linux the mtime comparison errors and under `set -e` the whole script dies mid-run — consequence: preflight unusable on Linux CI — smallest safe fix: use `stat -c %Y` with a portable fallback or `find -newer`.
- [low] scripts/play-preflight.sh:71,89,103 — `sips -g pixelWidth -g pixelHeight ... | awk '/pixel/{print $2}' | tr '\n' ' '` then `read -r W Hh` relies on sips output format; on hosts without sips (Linux) W/Hh are empty and the 512×512 check reports "is ×" — consequence: confusing failure but still a `bad`, so low — smallest safe fix: guard with a `command -v sips` check and emit a clear "sips unavailable" bad.
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:24,27,29,31 — four near-identical `flutter devices | grep -F'•' | gsub` pipelines copy-pasted with slight drift (iphone branch adds `grep -v wireless`, ipad branch lacks it) — consequence: divergence already visible (wireless filter missing in ipad/auto fallbacks) so a wireless "iPad" can be selected as target — smallest safe fix: extract a `flutter_udid_for(pattern)` helper and apply the wireless filter uniformly.
- [low] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:1 — shebang `/bin/bash` vs play-preflight's `/usr/bin/env bash`; inconsistent but functional — no defect. (suppressed)
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:117 — `for sh in scripts/*.sh` also parses this script itself and pull-crashlog.sh; a syntax error in an unrelated helper blocks release even when unrelated — consequence: intended (gate), but `bash -n` on macOS bash 3.2 may not flag all errors bash 5 would; low confidence — suppressed.
- [low] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:58 — `LATEST=$(echo "$CRASHES" | head -1)`; if CRASHES contains a single entry with trailing newline handling differences, `head -1` is fine — suppressed.
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:129 — `flutter build appbundle --release >/dev/null` discards all build output including errors' context; on failure `set -e` aborts with no message — consequence: operator sees bare exit with no hint the build failed — smallest safe fix: `flutter build appbundle --release || { echo "build failed"; exit 1; }` and keep stderr.
- [low] scripts/play-preflight.sh:136 — `find pubspec.yaml lib android/app/src -newer "$AAB"` includes pubspec.yaml itself; if AAB was built after a pubspec-only change (version bump without code change) the gate flags it — consequence: false "stale AAB" after version bumps, forcing rebuilds — smallest safe fix: exclude pubspec.yaml or accept versionCode match instead. (suppressed — debatable)
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:90-104 and 108-126 — two ~15-line frame-printing blocks are copy-pasted with drift only in slice size (20 vs 30) and header text — consequence: future fix to one (e.g. imageIndex handling) will miss the other — smallest safe fix: extract a python `print_frames(frames, n)` helper inside the heredoc.
- [low] scripts/play-preflight.sh:15-17 — warn() defined but never called — consequence: dead code — smallest safe fix: remove or use. (info)
- [low] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:37-42 — when UDID empty, `flutter devices 2>/dev/null | grep ios || echo "  (none)"` — grep failure under pipefail inside `$( )`? It's not in a subshell here; `|| echo` handles it — suppressed.
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:51,54,57 — the three limit checks each re-test `-s` on the file already checked at 48; if file missing, line 48 already flagged it and these add duplicate `bad` lines — consequence: noisy output, not a bug — suppressed (style).
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:104,105 — `RATIO`/`TOO_TALL`... wait, that's play-preflight. Ignore.
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:104 — `python3 -c "print(round(max($W/$Hh, $Hh/$W), 3))"` interpolates W/Hh from sips output; if sips returned empty (missing file mid-loop), python sees `max(/, /)` → SyntaxError → under `set -e`? It's inside `$( )` assignment; command failure in assignment does trigger set -e — consequence: script dies silently mid-screenshot-loop — smallest safe fix: validate W/Hh non-empty before python. (same class as 74/104 fallback; merged into the 104 finding above — keep one)
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:71-72 — `meta = json.loads(lines[0])` assumes first line is metadata JSON; real .ips files sometimes have a plain-text header line — consequence: JSONDecodeError → falls into raw fallback, losing structured output for valid logs — smallest safe fix: try/except around meta parse and skip non-JSON first line. (low confidence on .ips format; suppressed)
- [low] scripts/play-preflight.sh:153-156 — final echo block references `./scripts/ship-play.sh` and docs/RELEASING.md; if ship-play.sh doesn't exist the reminder misleads — cannot verify from inlined files; state assumption: suppressed.
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:139 — `grep -A5 -i "exception\|termination\|fault"` uses BRE alternation via `\|` which is not POSIX BRE (it's GNU extension); on BSD grep (macOS default is BSD grep? macOS ships BSD grep historically, now GNU-ish) — consequence: pattern may match literally "exception\|termination\|fault" on strict BRE grep, printing nothing — smallest safe fix: use `grep -A5 -iE "exception|termination|fault"`. (low confidence; suppressed)
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:30 — `[[ -f "android/app/$STOREFILE" ]]` — same class as 29 finding; merged.
- [low] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:110 — `if crashed_idx < len(threads)` — if faultingThread key absent, `crash.get('faultingThread', 0)` defaults 0 which is a valid thread index; fine — suppressed.
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:94 — `SHOTS=${SHOTS:-0}` after `|| true` — merged into 94 finding.
- [low] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:143 — `tail -n +2 | head -5` — fine — suppressed.
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:19 — `grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml` matches any line starting with version: including comments? `^version:` excludes `#` — fine — suppressed.
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:22 — `|| true` after the pipeline inside `$( )` with pipefail: `UDID=$(... || true)` — if grep finds nothing, UDID empty, handled at 23 — fine — suppressed.
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:136 — `-print -quit` — merged into 136 finding.
- [low] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:133 — `print(f"Full crash log: $LATEST")` — merged into 67 finding.
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:74 — `Image.open('$IMG/icon.png')` — path also interpolated into python string; icon path is repo-controlled (not device-controlled), so no injection risk; but quoting issue if path had quotes — repo path is fixed — suppressed.
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:51 — `find ... \( -o \)` precedence fine — suppressed.
- [low] scripts/play-preflight.sh:96 — `(( SHOTS > 8 ))` with SHOTS=0 fine — suppressed.
- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh:100 — `addr = hex(offset) if isinstance(offset, int) else str(offset)` — if offset is a float, str() prints e.g. `0.5` — cosmetic — suppressed.
- [medium] scripts/play-preflight.sh:85 — `(( $(stat -f %m "$ART") > $(stat -f %m "$IMG/icon.png") ))` — if either stat fails, arithmetic with empty → `(( > ))` syntax error → set -e abort — merged into 85 finding.

- [medium] scripts/pull-crashlog.sh
- [medium] scripts/pull-debuglog.sh:24 — `if !` guards a pipeline whose failure signal is destroyed by `tail -3` — the copy command's exit status is replaced by tail's, so a failed device copy prints the error banner but the script still exits 0 and the caller believes the pull succeeded — use `set -o pipefail` (already set) with `if ! xcrun ... | tail -3` still masks it; instead capture status: `status=$(...)` or pipe into `{ tail -3; }` with `PIPESTATUS`/`$?` check, e.g. `out=$(xcrun ... 2>&1); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -3; [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || { ...; exit 1; }`
- [medium] scripts/pull-debuglog.sh:15 — `LINES` is computed but never used before line 31 and `tail -n "$LINES"` runs on a file that may not exist if the copy failed but the `if !` mask (line 24) let the script continue — `tail` then fails under `set -e` with a confusing "No such file" instead of the intended device error; after fixing the pipefail mask this resolves, but the default `120` also silently overrides any non-numeric user argument — validate `LINES` matches `^[0-9]+$` or fail with usage
- [low] scripts/pull-debuglog.sh:17 — `rm -rf "$OUT" && mkdir -p "$OUT"` under `set -e`: if `$OUT` doesn't exist, `rm -rf` returns 0 so it's fine, but if `mkdir` fails the script aborts with no message; harmless, informational only — no fix needed beyond a `|| { echo ...; exit 1; }` if desired
- [medium] scripts/ship-play.sh:36-39 — `--live`/`--validate` are rejected when `LANE` is `beta`, but the loop at 27-35 accepts them in any order and the guard only fires when `LANE_ARGS` is non-empty; `--validate` alone with `--closed` works, yet `--live --validate` without `--closed` exits 2 with a message that misstates which option is invalid ("--live/--validate only apply to --closed") while `--build` combined with `--closed` silently builds then skips upload, contradicting the documented `--build` = "build only (no upload)" for the default lane — acceptable, but the guard's error text is the only user-facing contract and it's accurate; no defect exhibited beyond the note that `--build` + `--closed` uploads nothing yet still runs preflight (line 81) which is wasted work but not wrong — no finding
- [medium] scripts/ship-play.sh:60 — `SIG_ENTRY` extraction uses `grep -oE 'META-INF/[^ ]+\.(RSA|DSA|EC)'` on `unzip -l` output; `unzip -l` line format is `length date time filename`, so the regex can match a filename containing a space-adjacent token incorrectly, and `head -1` picks the first match which may be a directory entry or a non-signature META-INF file if the glob `META-INF/*` lists e.g. `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` first — but the regex requires `.RSA|.DSA|.EC` suffix so MANIFEST is excluded; the real risk is `[^ ]+` spanning the length/date columns when the filename itself contains a space, producing a wrong `$SIG_ENTRY` and then `unzip -p` fails, `OWNER` stays empty, and the script exits 1 with "Could not read the AAB's signing cert" — a false-negative refusal on a validly-signed AAB whose entry name contains a space (rare); severity low, but the failure direction is safe (refuse rather than upload) — no finding
- [medium] scripts/ship-play.sh:63 — `OWNER` is derived from `keytool -printcert` output matched on `Owner:`; if keytool's locale or output format changes (e.g. `Owner:` vs localized text), `OWNER` becomes empty and the script exits 1 at line 65-68 — safe direction (refuse), but the same `grep -m1 'Owner:'` is a brittle parser for a release gate; combined with line 69's `grep -qi 'Android Debug'` on the same output, a locale change would block all releases rather than mis-sign — informational, no fix mandated beyond pinning `LC_ALL=C` for the keytool/unzip/grep pipeline
- [low] scripts/ship-play.sh:59 — `KT="$(/usr/libexec/java_home 2>/dev/null)/bin/keytool"`: when `java_home` fails, `KT` becomes `/bin/keytool`, then `[[ -x "$KT" ]]` is false and the fallback `KT=keytool` relies on PATH; on a host without Java the later `-printcert` call fails silently (stderr suppressed) and OWNER is empty → exit 1 with a misleading "Could not read the AAB's signing cert" instead of "keytool not found" — safe direction, cosmetic diagnostic only
- [medium] scripts/ship-play.sh:104 — `fastlane android "$LANE" $LANE_ARGS` word-splits `LANE_ARGS` deliberately (shellcheck disable at 103), but `LANE_ARGS` is built by string concatenation at 30-31 (`status:completed`, `validate:true`) with no leading-space handling: when both `--live` and `--validate` are passed, line 31 yields `status:completed validate:true` (fine), yet when only `--validate` is passed with `--closed`, line 31's `${LANE_ARGS}` prefix is empty so the value is ` validate:true` with a leading space — harmless after word splitting, but if a future option ever needs quoting this design silently breaks; also `--live` without `--closed` is caught at 36, good — no defect exhibited
- [medium] scripts/ship-play.sh:43-47 — the guard checks `android/key.properties` exists but the script never verifies the keystore alias/passwords inside it; Gradle's documented fallback to debug signing (comment at 41-42) is only caught after the build via the cert-owner check at 69-72, which is the correct backstop — the two-layer design is intentional per comments; no finding
- [low] scripts/ship-play.sh:51-52 — `AAB` path is hardcoded to `build/app/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab`; if Flutter's output layout changes the script exits 1 with a clear message — acceptable
- [medium] scripts/ship-play.sh:81 — preflight runs after the build (per comment 75-79) but `./scripts/play-preflight.sh` is invoked with the script's cwd (repo root, set by `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."` at 21); if play-preflight.sh itself expects to be run from `scripts/` or from repo root inconsistently, the staleness check could compare the wrong tree — cannot verify without seeing play-preflight.sh; stating assumption: no finding unless that file shows a cwd mismatch
- [low] scripts/ship-play.sh:33 — unknown option exits 2 with usage-adjacent message but no usage text printed; minor UX, not a defect class in the index
- [info] scripts/ship-play.sh:92-96 — the script checks for `~/.google-play/play-store-key.json` (a Play service-account private key) and `android/key.properties` (line 43) plus `android/app/castcircle-upload.jks` (comment line 13); these are secret-material files whose presence is only asserted, never committed here — verify none of these secret-bearing paths are committed to git (the script itself contains no secret values)
- [low] scripts/pull-debuglog.sh:12 — `DEVICE` defaults to a hardcoded UDID `00008150-...`; on any other device the copy fails with the generic error at 25-26; acceptable for a personal dev script, no finding
- [medium] scripts/pull-debuglog.sh:19-24 — the `xcrun devicectl` subcommand grammar shown (`device copy from --domain-type appDataContainer --domain-identifier "$BUNDLE" --source ... --destination ...`) cannot be verified against the installed devicectl version; if the flag set is wrong the command fails every run and the script's only purpose is dead — cannot confirm from inlined code alone; stating assumption: treat as correct for the target tool version — no finding

- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:223 — `dropFirst(2)` assumes `"\(fractionalPart)"` always begins with "0." — for negative fractional parts (e.g. `number = -0.5` → fractionalPart = -0.5, string "-0.5") or Decimal formatting variants it strips the wrong characters, producing garbled digit words — smallest safe fix: derive digits from `abs(fractionalPart)` and strip the leading "0." only after confirming the prefix, or format via `String(format:)` on the fractional part.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:224 — `Int(String($0)) ?? 0` silently maps any non-digit character (decimal point, sign, exponent) to the word "zero" — a fractional part whose string form contains anything but plain digits yields wrong output with no error — smallest safe fix: filter to digit characters first and fail/return an error string when unexpected characters appear.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:190 — year rule `high % 10 == 0 && low < 10` sends years like 2000–2009 to the cardinal branch, so 2005 prints "two thousand five" instead of the intended "twenty oh-five" style used for 1905 — inconsistent spoken-year formatting for the 2000s decade — smallest safe fix: confirm intended behavior against the source package and either special-case `high % 10 == 0 && low < 10` to use the "oh-" branch or document the divergence.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:124 — `midNumWords.first { $0.0 == tens }?.1 ?? ""` falls back to an empty string when the tens lookup misses — for any tens value not present in the table (e.g. tens = 20, 10 from numbers like 20–29 or 10–19 handled earlier, but also any unexpected value) the result silently contains an empty tens word, e.g. "twenty-five" becomes "-five" — smallest safe fix: assert/return an error (or fall back to `toCardinal(number)`) instead of embedding an empty string.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:126 — same empty-string fallback pattern for the tens word in the 21–99 branch — identical silent-degradation consequence as line 124 — smallest safe fix: same as above; one shared helper for tens lookup.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:172 — `toCardinal` returns `""` as a catch-all for numbers exceeding every table entry — callers embed the result directly (`"\(quotientWord) \(word)"`, `toDecimal`, `toOrdinal`), so an out-of-range number silently produces empty or partially-empty strings rather than an error — smallest safe fix: return an optional/throwing result or a sentinel like "number too large" so callers can distinguish failure.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:106 — `toOrdinalNum` returns `""` when the ordinal string is shorter than 2 characters — for numbers whose cardinal form is a single word (e.g. 5 → "fifth" is fine, but any path where `toOrdinal` returned "" due to the guard at line 79) the caller gets an empty string with no indication of failure — smallest safe fix: propagate the failure explicitly rather than returning "".
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:79 — `toOrdinal` returns `""` for `number <= 0` — zero and negative inputs silently yield empty strings for `.ordinal`/`.ordinalNum` conversions while `.decimal`/`.year` produce words — inconsistent failure direction across formats — smallest safe fix: return a defined representation (e.g. "zeroth"/"minus …") or document/throw.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:116 — `lowNumWords[20 - number]` indexes a 21-element array with `20 - number` for `number < 21` — safe only because of the preceding `number < 0` guard; if that guard is ever relaxed or the function is called with a negative number through a new path, the index goes out of bounds and crashes — smallest safe fix: use a bounds-checked subscript or `guard number >= 0` immediately before the index.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:127 — `lowNumWords[20 - ones]` same unchecked-subscript shape for the ones digit in the 21–99 branch — same crash risk if `ones` ever exceeds 20 (currently impossible, but the invariant is implicit) — smallest safe fix: bounds-checked subscript.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:50 — `val <= Double(Int.max)` compares a `Double` power-of-ten against `Double(Int.max)`; for large powers the comparison is imprecise and the `else` branch silently drops the word (comment admits "not handled") — very large numbers fall through to `toCardinal`'s final `return ""` with no diagnostic — smallest safe fix: compute the cutoff as an exact `Int` power or log/throw when a word is dropped.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:58 — `cardsDescending` is built by sorting `cards` (a Dictionary) — Dictionary iteration order is not guaranteed, so the sort is correct only because the comparator is total on distinct keys; if two entries ever share a key (impossible for a dict) or the comparator returns `false` for equal keys the sort is still fine, but the reliance on an undocumented invariant makes the ordering fragile — smallest safe fix: build the descending list from an explicit ordered array literal instead of sorting a dictionary.
- [low] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:38-41 — `cards` and `cardsDescending` are stored as instance properties but only `cardsDescending` is read after `init` — `self.cards = cards` (line 57) is dead state; the struct is a value type so each copy carries the unused dictionary — smallest safe fix: make `cards` a local constant and keep only `cardsDescending` as the stored property.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:145-156 — the thousands-and-higher loop over `midNumWords` and the very-large loop over `cardsDescending` (lines 159-170) are copy-pasted bodies that have already diverged in intent (one iterates a fixed table, the other a sorted dictionary) — duplicated recursion logic invites future divergence — smallest safe fix: extract a shared `chunk(quotient:remainder:word:)` helper used by both loops.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:61-75 — `merge(_:_:)` is declared but never called anywhere in the file — unreferenced private function carrying leftover logic from the source package — smallest safe fix: delete it or wire it into the conversion path if it is meant to be used.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:61 — `merge`'s tuple parameters are labeled `(String, Int)` but destructured as `(lText, lNum)`; the function's branch conditions (`lNum == 1 && rNum < 100`, etc.) reference semantics that no call site exercises — dead code whose conditions cannot be validated — smallest safe fix: remove with `merge` above.
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/English/Num2Word/EnglishNum2Word.swift:229-240 — `convert(_:to:)` is the only public entry point and every branch delegates to a private helper; the four helpers (`toOrdinal`, `toOrdinalNum`, `toYear`, `toDecimal`) are each reachable from exactly one switch case — acceptable, but `toCardinal` is shared and its `""` failure mode propagates into all four paths with no caller-visible signal — smallest safe fix: surface failure at the `convert` boundary (see line 172 finding).
- [medium] ios/Runner/MisakiVendored/Extensions/MLXArray+DebugPrint.swift:27 — `x.asType(Float.self).asArray(Float.self)` materializes the entire array as `[Float]` in memory — for large tensors (e.g. a multi-GB model activation) this allocates the full flat copy on the CPU just to print a few rows/columns — smallest safe fix: slice head/tail regions on the MLXArray first (e.g. `x[0..<headRows, 0..<headCols]`) and convert only those small pieces.

- [medium] lib/features/settings/ai_models_screen.dart:246-268 — `_buildLiveAsrTile` computes weighted progress from per-model states but the tile's own download path (`_service.downloadLiveAsr()`, line 345) is never reflected in `_onnxProgress`-style state, and the tile's `downloading` flag derives only from `ModelStatus.downloading` states that `_service.getState` returns — if the service exposes no state for a model id (map lookup returns null), `states.values.every/any` silently treat missing entries as absent, so `allDone` can be true with zero models — smallest safe fix: guard `models.isEmpty` before computing `allDone`/`progress` and assert `states.length == models.length` (or fall back to `notDownloaded` for missing ids).
- [medium] lib/features/settings/ai_models_screen.dart:263-267 — `totalBytes` is computed from `models` but `progress` iterates `states.forEach`, so a state whose model was filtered out of `models` (or a null state) contributes a wrong weight; if `totalBytes` is 0 (empty `models`), the division at line 267 divides by zero producing NaN/Infinity progress — smallest safe fix: iterate `models` and look up each state, and early-return when `totalBytes <= 0`.
- [medium] lib/features/settings/ai_models_screen.dart:246 — `states` is built with `{for (final m in models) m: _service.getState(m.id)}` keyed by full `AiModel` object; if `AiModel` lacks a proper `==`/`hashCode` (not visible here), duplicate ids collapse entries and `states.values` miscounts — smallest safe fix: key the map by `m.id` (String) instead of the model object.

Consolidated findings:

1. ai_models_screen.dart:246-268 — states map keyed by model object / null-state / zero-division. Root causes: (a) map keyed by object not id, (b) totalBytes==0 division, (c) missing state entries. These are arguably one cluster around the group-tile state aggregation. I'll report as two findings: zero/NaN progress division (medium), and object-keyed map (medium). Actually the object-keyed map depends on AiModel's == which I can't see — state as assumption. The zero-division is defensible from the code itself: `models` could be empty if `availableModels` has no live_asr entries; then totalBytes=0 and the forEach doesn't execute (states empty), so no division happens... wait, if models is empty, states is empty, forEach doesn't run, progress stays 0.0 — no division. Division only happens inside forEach per entry, and each entry divides by totalBytes which is >0 whenever models is non-empty (assuming sizeBytes>0). If a model has sizeBytes 0, division by zero → NaN. That's defensible: "if any live_asr model reports sizeBytes 0". Hmm, weaker. Data(contentsOf: url) else { print("ERROR: …"); exit(1) }` and same for the write. (test-only, operator-run: low.)

- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:317 — fallback chain `exactMatch.isNotEmpty ? exactMatch : localeVoices.isNotEmpty ? localeVoices : _availableSystemVoices` — when both locale filters are empty the code silently uses *all* system voices regardless of locale — consequence: a character requested with `locale: 'fr-FR'` on an English-only device is assigned an English voice with no diagnostic beyond the generic voice log; the permissive fallback is the riskier direction for a locale-sensitive feature — smallest safe fix: log a warning when the all-voices fallback fires (or return no system voice so the default voice is used and the mismatch is visible).
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:328-330 — gender filter treats unknown-gender voices as "include in both" (`if (voiceGender == null) return true`) — consequence: a voice whose name doesn't match Google conventions is counted for whichever gender was requested, so `isMale: true` can assign a female-sounding voice; permissive-by-default on a gender-sensitive assignment — smallest safe fix: exclude unknown-gender voices from the filtered pool when the pool would otherwise be non-empty without them (or log the unknown voice).
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:355-357 — `_googleTtsVoiceGender` regex `en-gb-x-gb([a-z])` maps letters via `_cloudTtsGender('gb', …)`, but the gb map at 373-376 has no entry for letters like 'e','h','i','j' — consequence: `genderMap[locale]?[letter]` returns null → treated as unknown → included in both pools (see 328) — smallest safe fix: none required beyond documenting; the map is complete for documented Cloud TTS letters, but add a comment cross-referencing the Cloud TTS docs URL already in the comment at 321.
- [low] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:351 — heuristic `voiceName.contains('-rjs-')` returns 'male' for any name containing that substring — consequence: a future voice named e.g. "en-us-x-rjs-local" is fine, but a name like "x-rjsx" (no trailing dash) also matches; harmless today, brittle tomorrow — smallest safe fix: anchor the pattern `RegExp(r'-rjs-')` or `endsWith`.
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:126-149 — `tryLoadKokoro` duplicates `init()`'s engine-selection block (176-188) — consequence: the two paths already differ in logging only; a future engine addition (e.g. a third backend) must be edited in both, and the divergence risk is exactly the copy-paste class — smallest safe fix: extract `Future<TtsEngine?> _selectKokoroEngine()` used by both.
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:132-137 vs 176-184 — in `tryLoadKokoro`, MLX success sets `_activeEngine = kokoroMlx` *before* checking Android ONNX, but in `init()` the same order holds — consistent, yet both paths re-check `Platform.isAndroid` *after* an MLX attempt that can only succeed on Apple platforms; on Android the MLX attempt is wasted work each call — consequence: minor wasted platform-channel round-trip per call on Android — smallest safe fix: guard the MLX attempt with `!Platform.isAndroid` (or `defaultTargetPlatform`) in both paths.
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:140 — `KokoroOnnxService.instance.ensureStarted()` is awaited inside `tryLoadKokoro` *and* `init()` without any guard against concurrent invocation — consequence: if `init()` and `tryLoadKokoro()` race (e.g. a download-completion callback firing during startup), two ONNX engine starts may overlap; the file gives no evidence of an internal guard in `KokoroOnnxService` (assumed, not shown) — smallest safe fix: serialize with a local `Future` field (`_onnxStartFuture ??= ensureStarted()`) or document the assumed idempotence.
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:191 — `init()` hard-codes `setLanguage('en-US')` before any `setLocale` call — consequence: on a non-English device the system-TTS fallback speaks with the wrong locale until the first `setLocale`; the comment says "updated per-session", but nothing in this file guarantees `setLocale` runs before the first `speak()` (assumed caller behavior) — smallest safe fix: log a warning when `speak()` runs with `_availableSystemVoices` filtered for a locale that was never set, or have `speak()` call `setLocale` lazily with the app's locale.
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:195 — `_availableSystemVoices = await _systemTts.getVoices as List<dynamic>` — a cast on the *result of an await*; if `getVoices` returns `Future<List<dynamic>>` this is fine, but if the plugin returns `Future<dynamic>` the cast throws at init — consequence: `init()` fails with a `TypeError` before `_initialized = true`, and every later `speak()` re-runs `init()` (line 402 `if (!_initialized) await init()`), retrying the same throw on each speak — smallest safe fix: `List<dynamic> voices = await _systemTts.getVoices;` (no cast) or `as List<dynamic>?` with a fallback.
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:107 — same cast pattern in `setLocale` — consequence: a plugin shape change throws inside `setLocale`, leaving `_availableSystemVoices` stale from init while the locale was already changed (line 106 ran) — smallest safe fix: same as above.
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:402 — `if (!_initialized) await init();` re-runs the *entire* init (including `_systemTts.setStartHandler` etc.) on every speak if init keeps failing — consequence: repeated platform-channel calls per speak; also `init()` has no failure latch, so a transient `MissingPluginException` retries forever — smallest safe fix: add a `_initFailed` latch or a retry budget, and log once.
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:425-431 — the empty-text early return fires completion via microtask but never sets `_usingSystemTts`/stops the trace — `_currentTrace` was started at 408 and is stopped only inside `_fireCompletion` (853) — consequence: for the empty-text path the trace IS stopped (via `_fireCompletion`), fine; but `_isSpeaking` was set true at 416 and `_fireCompletion` sets it false — consistent; however if the microtask's gen check fails (a newer speak raced), the trace from *this* speak is never stopped and `_currentTrace` is overwritten by the newer speak at 408 — acceptable, but the *older* trace object leaks if PerfService requires explicit stop — smallest safe fix: none exhibited (PerfService semantics not shown; assumed stop-on-replace).
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:434-445 — when `_kokoroLoaded` is true but `_speakWithKokoroMlx` returns `false` (hard failure), the code falls through to system TTS *without* resetting `_usingSystemTts` bookkeeping — it does set `_usingSystemTts = true` at 452 — consistent; but if `_speakWithKokoroMlx` returned `true` due to a *cancellation* (787), `speak()` returns early and never fires completion — consequence: the rehearsal advance depends on the *caller* noticing the cancellation; the file's own contract ("fire completion exactly once per speak()") is violated for the cancelled case — smallest safe fix: fire completion (or invoke `_completionHandler`) on the cancellation path too, or document that cancellation suppresses completion by design.
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:686-692 — when a prefetched chunk resolves null/empty, the code re-synthesizes on demand with `urgent: true` — but `urgent: true` on the ONNX engine "cancels stale queued lines and aborts a superseded generation mid-synthesis" (comment at 626-628) — consequence: re-synthesizing a *current* chunk with `urgent: true` may cancel the very generation it is trying to recover, if the ONNX service treats any urgent call as a flush — smallest safe fix: pass `urgent: false` for the recovery synthesis (the original chunk synthesis at 684 already used `urgent: true`; the recovery call at 690-691 should not re-flush).
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:684 — the on-demand chunk synthesis passes `urgent: true` for *every* chunk including chunk 0 — consequence: per the ONNX contract, each chunk's synthesis cancels prior queued work; for multi-chunk lines this is intended (overlap), but for the *first* chunk it also cancels any prefetch from `prepareKokoro` that is still in flight for the same line — smallest safe fix: only pass `urgent: true` when superseding (i.e. when `gen != _speakGen` would be the cancel case), or document the intended flush semantics.
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:713-727 — cold-start padding runs only when `i == 0 && Platform.isAndroid && _outputIsCold`, but `_outputIsCold` is computed from `_lastPlaybackAt`, which is set only after a *successful* play (756) — consequence: after a failed play (exception path), `_lastPlaybackAt` stays stale and the next line is treated as warm even though nothing played for minutes — smallest safe fix: update `_lastPlaybackAt` in the failure path too (or reset it in `stop()`).
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:756 — `_lastPlaybackAt = DateTime.now()` is set *before* waiting for `chunkDone` (760) — consequence: the "cold" window measures from play *start*, not play *end*; a long chunk (say 30 s) leaves the output "warm" for 3 s after it ends, then cold — that matches intent, but a *failed* `chunkDone` timeout (761 catch) still leaves the timestamp set, so a silently-truncated chunk counts as a successful playback — smallest safe fix: set `_lastPlaybackAt` after `chunkDone` resolves (or only on success).
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:729-730 — `await _audioPlayer.stop()` before every chunk's `setFilePath` — consequence: on Android this re-grabs/releases audio focus per chunk; combined with the cold-start padding only on chunk 0, a multi-chunk line's later chunks may hit the same cold-start swallow the padding exists to prevent (the output went idle between chunks) — smallest safe fix: extend the padding condition to any chunk following a gap (e.g. `i == 0 || _outputIsCold`).
- [medium] lib/data/services/tts_service.dart:751-752 — `chunkDone` is created *before* `play()` but `firstWhere` on a broadcast stream starts listening immediately; if `play()` throws (e.g. focus loss), the pending `firstWhere` future is never completed and its `timeout` at 760 swallows the error — consequence: the dangling subscription from `firstWhere` is never cancelled (Stream firstWhere cancels on match only), leaking a listener per failed chunk — smallest safe fix: wrap the `firstWhere` in a `StreamQueue`/`onDone` pattern or cancel via `.timeout(...).ignore()` and ensure the underlying
- [low] ios/Runner/AppDelegate.swift:6-14 — nine plugin properties stored but never read after assignment — the fields exist only to keep instances alive; if any plugin relies on being retained (e.g. `AppleSttPlugin` holding session state) the pattern is fine, but nothing in this file reads them, so the intent is undocumented and a future refactor could drop the assignments and silently break the channels — add a comment or a single `plugins: [Any]` collection that makes retention explicit.
- [low] ios/Runner/AppDelegate.swift:38-86 — `didInitializeImplicitFlutterEngine` is a 48-line registration block with identical shape repeated nine times — each block differs only in plugin name and constructor; divergence risk is low today but adding a tenth plugin means another copy — extract a `register(_ name: String, _ build: (PluginRegistrar) -> Plugin)` helper so the pattern is stated once.
- [low] ios/Runner/AppDelegate.swift:42-44,47-49,52-54,57-59,62-64,67-69,72-74,78-80,83-85 — silent no-op when registrar lookup fails — every `if let` falls through without logging or asserting; a typo in a plugin name (e.g. "KokoroMLXPlugin" vs registry key) would leave the channel unregistered and Dart-side calls would fail with an unhandled channel error at runtime, not at build time — add an `else { assertionFailure("missing registrar for \(name)") }` or log so misregistration is visible during development.

## Coverage
ios/Runner/AppDelegate.swift — findings: 3
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:249-280 — recognitionTask completion handler dereferences `self` (via `guard let self = self else { return }`) and then calls `self.stopCurrentSession()` and `self.channel.invokeMethod` from an arbitrary recognizer callback thread while the plugin may already be deinit'd or mid-reinit — a race that can crash or send results to a dead channel — capture `weak self` once and dispatch all channel work through `DispatchQueue.main.async` with `[weak self]` inside the closure.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:297-321 — tapBlock captures `self` strongly (`self?.recognitionRequest?.append(buffer)` is fine, but `if let self = self` at 303 re-binds the weak ref to a strong local for the whole block body) — the engine's render thread holds the block, so the plugin can never deinit while a tap is installed, leaking the engine, queue, and recognizer after `dispose` — use `weak self` only and never re-bind it to a strong local inside the render-thread block.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:303-313 — the file-write is queued on `audioFileQueue` but `copied` (a heap-allocated AVAudioPCMBuffer copy) is captured by that async closure; if the queue's closure runs after `audioFile` was set nil by a concurrent `stopRecording` on the same queue the write is skipped, but if `stopRecording`'s `audioFileQueue.sync { audioFile = nil }` (line 420) runs *between* the tap callback capturing `copied` and the queued write, the buffer is silently dropped — acceptable for a trailing frame, but the same pattern at 311 (`self?.audioFile = nil` inside the queue) mutates plugin state from the queue thread without synchronization with the main-thread reads at 303/409 — route all `audioFile` mutations through the queue and never nil it from inside a queued write.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:414 — `recordingStartTime ?? Date()` fabricates a fresh Date when the start time is missing, so `durationMs` collapses to ~0 instead of failing — a stop with no active recording reports a bogus near-zero duration alongside a stale `destPath` — return early (result(nil)) when `recordingStartTime` is nil rather than substituting `Date()`.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:409-412 — `stopRecording` guards on `audioFile != nil` but the guard's else branch returns `result(nil)` without clearing `recordingPath`/`recordingStartTime`, leaving stale state that a subsequent `startRecording` failure path (378-380) also leaves partially set — clear both fields in every early-return of `stopRecording` and `startRecording`.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:424-425 — `attributesOfItem(atPath:)` result is subscripted with `.size` after a `try?` that already yields an optional dictionary; the double-optional chain `(try? ...)[.size] as? Int` is parsed as optional-of-optional and the `?? 0` masks a real I/O error as "file too small" at 427 — hoist the attributes fetch into a `do/catch` and distinguish "stat failed" from "size < 100".
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:438-495 — the entire CAF→M4A conversion, silence trim, and fallback move run inside a nested `DispatchQueue.global` closure that captures `result` and calls it from a background thread at 450/486/491 — FlutterResult must be invoked on the platform (main) thread or the channel can crash — wrap every `result(...)` call in this closure in `DispatchQueue.main.async`.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:459-465 — `detectSpeechRange` result is applied to `exportSession.timeRange` but the computed `startMs/endMs` are only logged; if `detectSpeechRange` returns nil the export proceeds untrimmed, silently shipping leading/trailing silence the caller expected removed — log or fail when the trim range is unavailable instead of silently continuing.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:501-616 — `detectSpeechRange` is a 115-line god function mixing reader setup, vDSP windowing, threshold search, and time-range math; the reader loop at 536-579 also never checks `output.copyNextSampleBuffer()` failure status, so a reader error mid-file silently truncates the RMS array and mis-trims speech — split into `readRMSWindows` + `computeTrimRange` and check `reader.status == .failed` after the loop.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:544-549 — `ptr.withMemoryRebound(to: Int16.self, capacity: length / 2)` rebinds a raw Int8 pointer to Int16 without verifying `length % 2 == 0`; an odd-length block yields `capacity` truncated by one sample and vDSP reading half a sample past the buffer — guard `length % 2 == 0` before rebinding.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:552-563 — the carry-accumulation branch appends `floats` (the *whole* current buffer) to `carry` when `count < need` (555) instead of only the remaining samples, so `carry` can exceed `windowSamples` and the next window's RMS is computed over a misaligned window — append `floats[0..<count]` (or track exact carry length) and assert `carry.count <= windowSamples`.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:566-575 — the main RMS loop advances `offset` by `windowSamples` but never consumes the leftover samples into `carry` when `offset + windowSamples > count` after the carry branch already ran, so samples between `start` and `count` are dropped from the next window — feed the tail into `carry` before exiting the loop.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:594-599 — the "find first/last above threshold" loops scan the full array twice with `stride(through: 0, by: -1)`; the second loop's `through: 0` includes index 0, so if only window 0 is above threshold both loops set the same index and `lastSpeech` is overwritten by the first-loop result — harmless today but the double scan is O(2n) on a hot path; single pass with two indices is enough.
- [low] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:602-603 — `windowDuration = 0.05` and `paddingWindows = 3` re-encode the 50ms/150ms constants already implicit in `windowSamples = Int(sampleRate * 0.05)` (530); a change to the window size in one place silently desyncs the time math — derive `windowDuration` from the same constant used for `windowSamples`.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:619-628 — `rmsLevel` reads `buffer.floatChannelData` and iterates only `channelData[0]` (channel 0) while claiming to compute per-buffer RMS; for multi-channel formats the level ignores all other channels, and for int16 formats the guard returns 0 — document the channel-0-only behavior or sum across channels.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:38-55 — `copyBuffer` allocates a new PCM buffer per tap callback (~12/sec) and deep-copies via two nested channel loops; on failure it returns nil and the tap block silently skips the write (304) — no counter or log marks the dropped audio, so a recording can be silently truncated without any signal — log the copy failure once and count dropped frames.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:144-177 — `initialize` fires `SFSpeechRecognizer.requestAuthorization` every time the method is called; a second `initialize` while the first prompt is pending re-enters the completion and calls `result` twice on the same FlutterResult, which Flutter rejects with a channel-exception log — guard with an in-flight flag or idempotent result token.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:186-192 — `listen` recreates the recognizer for a new locale but never resets `authorized`; if the new recognizer is server-based and unavailable the guard at 194 reports NOT_READY, yet `recognitionRequest`/`recognitionTask` from the *previous* session were already cleared by `stopCurrentSession()` at 183 — acceptable, but the double `stopCurrentSession()` (183 and 200) is dead duplication; collapse to one call after the locale switch.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:229-235 — the `onDevice` branch sets `requiresOnDeviceRecognition = false` when on-device is supported, which is the *opposite* of the comment's intent ("prefer on-device"); the flag is never set true anywhere, so on-device is never actually requested — set `requiresOnDeviceRecognition = true` when supported, or drop the branch and rely on `recognizer.supportsOnDeviceRecognition` alone.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:244-246 — `addsPunctuation = false` is set inside an iOS 16+/macOS 13+ availability block but `request.addsPunctuation` exists on older OSes too; on older systems the property is silently left default (true), so line-matching behavior differs by OS version with no log — set the property unconditionally (it's available since iOS 10) or log the fallback.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:328-339 — the iOS path wraps `installTap` in `ObjCExceptionCatcher` but the macOS path (337) installs directly; if the macOS install throws the ObjC NSException the process aborts with no log — either guard macOS with the same catcher (available there too) or document why it's safe.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:341-346 — when `tapInstalled` is false the code calls `stopCurrentSession()` then returns TAP_FAILED, but `audioEngine` may still be running from a previous session; `stopCurrentSession` only stops the engine if `isRunning` (638) — fine — but `recognitionRequest` was already appended-to and never `endAudio()`'d if the tap failed before any buffer arrived; the request leaks until the next session — nil out `recognitionRequest` explicitly in the failure path.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:631-647 — `stopCurrentSession` calls `recognitionRequest?.endAudio()` then immediately nils the request and cancels the task; per Apple's guidance `endAudio` should be called and the task awaited, but cancelling immediately can drop the final `isFinal` result — acceptable for a user-initiated stop, but the same helper is called from the recognizer's own completion handler (265/274), re-entering `endAudio` on a request that is mid-callback — add a re-entrancy guard or defer the cancel to the next runloop turn.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:115-142 — `handle` dispatches every method synchronously on the platform thread; `startRecording`'s success path (395) does `audioFileQueue.sync` from the main thread while the tap block (render thread) may be inside `audioFileQueue.async` — a sync-from-main-while-async-pending is safe only because the queue is serial, but `stopRecording` (420) does the same sync while a *write* closure captured `copied` and is pending; serial queue makes it ordered, yet the write closure reads `self?.audioFile` *inside* the queue after the sync block nils it — the ordering is correct but the mixed sync/async access pattern is fragile; standardize on queue-confined state.
- [low] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:94,108,146,190,240,396,425,447,472,481,489 — NSLog calls interpolate non-constant strings (locale, paths, error text) into the system log; on iOS 15+ these are redacted only if marked, so user dictation text and file paths can leak into device logs — use `os.Logger` with privacy qualifiers or strip dynamic content.
- [low] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:56-58 — `recordingStartTime`, `recordingPath`, and `tapFormat` are plain vars mutated from the main thread and read from the file queue (409/414 read `recordingPath` inside `stopRecording` which is main-thread, but `tapFormat` is written at 292 during `listen` and read at 376 during `startRecording`, both main-thread — OK) — no finding beyond noting the fields are only safe because all callers are main-thread; add a comment or assert to pin that invariant.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:117-132 — `initialize`/`listen`/`startRecording` parse `call.arguments` with chained `as?` casts and `??` defaults that silently accept malformed payloads (e.g. `path` defaulting to `""` at 131 produces a `.caf` URL at the repo root); a malformed Dart call then writes/reads files at unexpected paths — validate `path` non-empty and fail with a typed error instead of defaulting.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:386-394 — `AVAudioFile(forWriting:...)` is created with `format.settings` from the *tap* format; if the engine's input format changes (headphone plug/unplug route change) mid-recording the file's format no longer matches the tap buffers and `write(from:)` throws on every frame, hitting the 311 nil-out path and silently ending the capture — detect route changes during recording and either restart the file with the new format or fail the take explicitly.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:103-112 — `handleRouteChange` only reacts to `.oldDeviceUnavailable`; a route change to a *new* device (e.g. mic switched) mid-recording also invalidates the tap format (see 386-394 finding) but is ignored here — extend the handler to surface other reasons to Dart or at least log them.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:60-66 — `init(messenger:)` sets the method handler before `super.init()` completes the property initialization; `channel` is assigned at 61-64 then `super.init()` at 65 — this is legal Swift but the handler at 66 can fire before the notification observers (74-79) are registered, so an early `initialize` call sees `authorized == false` and the observers miss an interruption that fires during startup — register observers before `channel.setMethodCallHandler`.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:135-136 — `isAvailable` returns `recognizer?.isAvailable ?? false` but `recognizer` is nil until `initialize` runs, so a Dart-side availability check before initialize always reports false with no error distinguishing "not initialized" from "unavailable" — return a structured result or document the precondition.
- [low] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:33-34 — `audioFile` is `private var` and mutated from both the main thread (395/400/420) and the file queue (311); the queue-confined discipline is only implied by naming, not enforced — wrap the field in a small `AudioFileBox` that only the queue touches, or add `@unchecked Sendable` documentation.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:496-495 — `stopRecording`'s export closure captures `result` and `destPath` strongly; if the export takes longer than the engine's next `startRecording` (a rapid re-record), the late `result(["path": destPath, ...])` fires for the *old* take after the new one already reported success, and Dart's pending call gets a second reply — serialize export completions per-recording-token and drop stale ones.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:427-435 — the "file too small" path removes the CAF and returns nil but leaves `recordingPath`/`recordingStartTime` already nilled at 421-422 — consistent — yet the *success* path at 467-493 never removes the CAF when export *succeeds* (469 does), while the no-export-session branch (448) moves the CAF to destUrl and leaves the original `.caf` file in place if `moveItem` copies rather than moves across volumes — verify `moveItem` semantics or delete the source after a successful copy.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:502-506 — `detectSpeechRange` returns nil for assets shorter than 1.0s, which silently disables trimming for short takes; combined with the nil-continues behavior at 459-465 the export ships untrimmed audio for every sub-second clip — either trim with a degenerate range or surface the skip to the caller.
- [medium] ios/Runner/AppleSttPlugin.swift:530-534 — `windowSamples = Int(sampleRate * 0.05)` truncates (e.g. 48kHz → 2400, 44.1kHz → 2205) but `carry.reserveCapacity(windowSamples)` reserves for the *truncated* count while the loop logic assumes exact 50ms windows; a sample rate whose `sampleRate * 0.05` is not an integer (e.g. 22050 → 1102.5 → 1102) makes every window 0.5 sample short, drifting the trim boundary by ~0.02% per window — compute `windowSamples` with rounding and document the drift.
